knowledge_statements.title: Polarity-Gauge Theory
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional polarity and the extended-valued gauge–support correspondence for closed convex sets containing the origin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, and let \(C\subseteq X\) be nonempty, closed, convex, and contain \(0\). Define
\[
C^\circ=\{y\in X:\langle y,c\rangle\leq 1\ \text{for every }c\in C\},\qquad
\gamma_C(x)=\inf\{t\geq 0:x\in tC\},
\]
with the infimum of the empty set equal to \(+\infty\). Then, for every \(x\in X\),
\[
\gamma_C(x)=\sigma_{C^\circ}(x)=\sup_{y\in C^\circ}\langle x,y\rangle,
\qquad C^{\circ\circ}=C.
\]
Thus the gauge of \(C\) is represented by the support function of its polar, while polarity recovers \(C\) under the stated closure and convexity assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex set containing zero equals its bipolar, and its possibly infinite gauge equals the support function of its polar set.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.
\(C\subseteq X\) is nonempty, closed, convex, and satisfies \(0\in C\).

notation.meaning: The polar set of C with unit upper bound under the inner product.
The extended-valued Minkowski gauge of C.
The support function of a set D.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support Function of a Nonempty Set
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(E=\mathbb{R}^n\) be equipped with an inner product \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle\), and let \(S\subset E\) be nonempty. The codomain is the extended real line \(\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is the finite-dimensional support function of an arbitrary nonempty set. Convexity, closedness, boundedness, and attainment are not assumed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The support function of \(S\) is the map
\[
\sigma_S:E\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\},\qquad \sigma_S(d):=\sup_{s\in S}\langle s,d\rangle .
\]
Its effective domain is
\[
\operatorname{dom}\sigma_S:=\{d\in E:\sigma_S(d)<+\infty\}.
\]
Thus \(d\in\operatorname{dom}\sigma_S\) exactly when \(S\) is contained in a halfspace \(\{s:\langle s,d\rangle\le r\}\) for some \(r\in\mathbb{R}\). The function is positively homogeneous and subadditive:
\[
\sigma_S(td)=t\sigma_S(d)\quad(t\ge0),\qquad
\sigma_S(d_1+d_2)\le\sigma_S(d_1)+\sigma_S(d_2).
\]
It is a closed convex function, satisfies \(\sigma_S(0)=0\), and depends only on the closed convex hull:
\[
\sigma_S=\sigma_{\operatorname{cl}S}=\sigma_{\operatorname{co}S}=\sigma_{\overline{\operatorname{co}}S}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each direction, the support function is the supremum over the set of the corresponding linear functional. Its finite-value domain consists precisely of directions in which the set has a finite upper supporting level. It is closed, convex, positively homogeneous, and subadditive, and replacing the set by its closure, convex hull, or closed convex hull does not change it.
assumptions_latex: \(E=\mathbb{R}^n\) has the fixed inner product used to identify directions with linear functionals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_S(d)=\sup_{s\in S}\langle s,d\rangle\), with \(\sigma_S\) closed and sublinear and \(\sigma_S=\sigma_{\overline{\operatorname{co}}S}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}\sigma_S=\{(d,r):\langle s,d\rangle\le r\ \forall s\in S\}\).
\(d\in\operatorname{dom}\sigma_S\iff \exists r\in\mathbb{R}\text{ such that }S\subseteq\{s:\langle s,d\rangle\le r\}\).
special_cases_latex: For \(S=\{s_0\}\), \(\sigma_S(d)=\langle s_0,d\rangle\).
For the Euclidean unit ball \(B\), \(\sigma_B(d)=\|d\|\).
immediate_consequences_latex: \(S\subseteq T\Rightarrow\sigma_S\le\sigma_T\).
Support data cannot distinguish a nonconvex or nonclosed set from its closed convex hull.
boundary_notes: The supremum may equal \(+\infty\).
A finite supremum need not be attained unless additional compactness or coercivity is available.
The definition depends on the chosen dual pairing.

notation.meaning: support function of the nonempty set S

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support Functional of a Convex Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition on the continuous dual of a real normed vector space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\) be a convex subset of a real normed vector space \(X\). The support functional of \(K\) is the functional \(h\) on \(X^*\) defined by
\[
h(x^*)=\sup_{x\in K}\langle x,x^*\rangle.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex set K in a real normed vector space X, its support functional maps each continuous linear functional x* to the supremum of its pairing with points of K.
assumptions_latex: X\text{ is a real normed vector space}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Supporting Levels, Hyperplanes, and Contact Sets
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, let \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and write \(\sigma_C(d)=\sup_{x\in C}\langle x,d\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition covers arbitrary nonempty sets and distinguishes finite support, supporting hyperplanes, and actual contact. No convexity or compactness is needed to define these objects.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A direction \(d\) is a finite support direction for \(C\) when \(\sigma_C(d)<+\infty\). For such \(d\), define the supporting halfspace, supporting level hyperplane, and support-point set by
\[
H_C^-(d):=\{x:\langle x,d\rangle\le\sigma_C(d)\},
\]
\[
H_C(d):=\{x:\langle x,d\rangle=\sigma_C(d)\},
\qquad
M_C(d):=C\cap H_C(d)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in C}\langle x,d\rangle.
\]
Then \(C\subseteq H_C^-(d)\), and \(\sigma_C(d)\) is the least real number \(r\) such that \(C\subseteq\{x:\langle x,d\rangle\le r\}\). The hyperplane supports \(C\) in direction \(d\) precisely when \(M_C(d)\neq\varnothing\). For \(t>0\),
\[
H_C(td)=H_C(d),\qquad M_C(td)=M_C(d),
\]
so the geometry depends on the oriented ray generated by \(d\), not its positive normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite support direction is one in which the set has a finite maximal linear value. That value is the smallest upper halfspace threshold containing the set. The boundary hyperplane at that threshold is supporting only when it meets the set, and its contact set is exactly the set of maximizers. Positive rescaling of a nonzero direction leaves the hyperplane and contact set unchanged.
assumptions_latex: For the displayed hyperplane and contact-set definitions, \(d\in\operatorname{dom}\sigma_C\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(x\in M_C(d)\iff x\in C\text{ and }\langle x,d\rangle\ge\langle y,d\rangle\ \forall y\in C\).
\(M_C(d)\neq\varnothing\iff \sup_{x\in C}\langle x,d\rangle\text{ is attained}\).
special_cases_latex: If \(C\) is compact, then \(M_C(d)\neq\varnothing\) for every \(d\).
With the convention \(M_C(0)=C\), the zero direction exposes the whole set.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(C\) is convex, then every nonempty \(M_C(d)\) is convex.
If \(C\) is closed and \(\sigma_C(d)<+\infty\), the contact set is closed, although it may still be empty.
boundary_notes: Finite support does not imply attainment for an unbounded closed convex set.
If \(\sigma_C(d)=+\infty\), there is no finite supporting level orthogonal to \(d\).
Directions \(d\) and \(-d\) represent opposite orientations and generally produce different support levels.

notation.meaning: minimal closed halfspace with outward normal d containing C
support-point or contact set in direction d

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_C(u)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in C}\langle u,x\rangle\), with \(S_C(u)\neq\varnothing\) exactly when the support supremum is attained.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The support-point set of \(C\) in direction \(u\) is \[S_C(u):=\{x\in C:\langle u,x\rangle=h_C(u)\}=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in C}\langle u,x\rangle.\] Thus \(S_C(u)\) is nonempty exactly when the defining supremum is attained. If \(C\) is compact, then \(S_C(u)\) is nonempty and compact for every \(u\); if \(C\) is also convex, it is a face of \(C\). For a general closed convex set, a finite value \(h_C(u)\) need not imply attainment, so \(S_C(u)\) may be empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Support points maximize a linear functional over the set. Compactness guarantees attainment; closedness alone does not.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive rescaling and the zero-direction regime for support-point sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty and let \(S_C(u)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in C}\langle u,x\rangle\). For every \(\alpha>0\), \[S_C(\alpha u)=S_C(u),\] including simultaneous emptiness when the supremum is not attained. Moreover, \[S_C(0)=C.\] Thus, for \(u\ne0\), the support-point set depends only on the positive ray generated by \(u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive rescaling does not change a support-point set, while the zero direction selects the entire set.

notation.meaning: Support-point set of C in direction u.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Incidence Between Exposed Faces and Normal Directions
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty closed convex set. For \(x\in C\), define \(N_C(x):=\{d:\langle y-x,d\rangle\le0\ \forall y\in C\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is finite-dimensional closed convex geometry. Empty exposed faces are allowed when a finite support value is not attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\), define the face exposed by \(d\) as
\[
F_C(d):=\{x\in C:\langle x,d\rangle=\sigma_C(d)\}.
\]
For \(d\neq0\), every nonempty \(F_C(d)\) is an exposed face of \(C\); set \(F_C(0):=C\). The face-direction incidence relation is
\[
\mathcal I_C:=\{(x,d)\in C\times\mathbb{R}^n:x\in F_C(d)\}.
\]
It has the equivalent normal-cone description
\[
(x,d)\in\mathcal I_C
\iff \langle y-x,d\rangle\le0\quad\forall y\in C
\iff d\in N_C(x).
\]
For a nonempty exposed face \(F\) of \(C\), its exposing-direction cone is
\[
D_C(F):=\{d:F_C(d)=F\}.
\]
Thus \(F_C(d)\) records all points incident to the supporting direction \(d\), while \(N_C(x)\) records all supporting directions incident to the point \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point and a direction are incident when the point maximizes the direction's linear functional over the set. Equivalently, the direction belongs to the normal cone at the point. Fixing the direction gives an exposed face; fixing the point gives its cone of supporting directions. Directions exposing exactly a prescribed face form that face's exposing-direction set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in F_C(d)\iff d\in N_C(x)\), where \(F_C(d)=\{x\in C:\langle x,d\rangle=\sigma_C(d)\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(x\in F_C(d)\iff \langle x,d\rangle=\sup_{y\in C}\langle y,d\rangle\).
\(x\in F_C(d)\iff C\subseteq\{y:\langle y,d\rangle\le\langle x,d\rangle\}\).
special_cases_latex: \(F_C(0)=C\) and \(N_C(x)\) always contains \(0\).
If \(F_C(d)=\{x\}\), then \(x\) is an exposed point.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every nonempty \(F_C(d)\) is a face of \(C\).
If \(x\in\operatorname{int}C\), then \(N_C(x)=\{0\}\).
boundary_notes: A face need not be exposed.
For an unbounded set, a direction may have finite support but no incident point.
The set \(D_C(F)\) uses equality of exposed faces, whereas \(\bigcap_{x\in F}N_C(x)\) also contains directions exposing a larger face.

notation.meaning: face of C exposed by d
convex-analytic normal cone to C at x

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonempty subset \(F\subseteq C\) is an exposed face of \(C\) if there exists \(u\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}\) such that \[F=F_C(u):=\{x\in C:\langle u,x\rangle=h_C(u)\}.\] Equivalently, \(F\) is the intersection of \(C\) with a supporting hyperplane having outward normal \(u\). Every exposed face is a face of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exposed face is the set of maximizers of one nonzero linear functional over a convex set, and every exposed face is a face.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Planar compact convex example separating extreme and exposed points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^2:\|x\|_2\leq1\}\), \(a=(2,0)\), and \(C=\operatorname{conv}(B\cup\{a\})\). For \(p=(1/2,\sqrt3/2)\), the singleton \(\{p\}\) is an extreme face of \(C\), but it is not exposed: the supporting line of \(B\) at \(p\) also contains \(a\), and its contact set with \(C\) is \([p,a]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tangency point where a disk joins an exterior apex is extreme but not exposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{p\}\) is an extreme face of \(C\) but is not exposed.
knowledge_statements.title: Extreme Need Not Mean Exposed

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Density of exposed points among extreme points in finite-dimensional compact convex sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, compact, and convex, then \[\operatorname{ext}C\subseteq\overline{\operatorname{exp}C}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every extreme point of a compact convex set is a limit of exposed points.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonzero vector \(u\in\mathbb{R}^n\) exposes \(F\) when \[F=F_C(u):=\{x\in C:\langle u,x\rangle=h_C(u)\}.\] The exposing-direction set is \[E_C(F):=\{u\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}:F_C(u)=F\}.\] It is positively homogeneous: if \(u\in E_C(F)\) and \(\lambda>0\), then \(\lambda u\in E_C(F)\). Hence an exposing direction represents a ray of equivalent supporting normals rather than a distinguished normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exposing direction is a nonzero normal whose maximizing set is exactly the given exposed face; positive rescaling preserves it.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex, let \(F\) be a nonempty proper exposed face, and choose \(x\in\operatorname{ri}F\). Then \[E_C(F)=\operatorname{ri}N_C(x).\] Thus the exposing directions form a relatively open convex cone and do not depend on the chosen \(x\in\operatorname{ri}F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Directions exposing a proper face are exactly the relative-interior directions of the normal cone along that face.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a nonempty proper exposed face of \(C\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common-normal extension of point incidence and its order reversal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty subset \(F\subseteq C\), define \(N_C(F):=\bigcap_{x\in F}N_C(x)\). Then, for every \(u\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \[u\in N_C(F)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad F\subseteq F_C(u).\] Consequently, if \(F\subseteq G\subseteq C\), then \(N_C(G)\subseteq N_C(F)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A direction is normal at every point of a subset exactly when its support face contains that subset; inclusion reverses common-normal inclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u\in N_C(F)\iff F\subseteq F_C(u)\), and \(F\subseteq G\Rightarrow N_C(G)\subseteq N_C(F)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Setwise Face–Normal Incidence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common-normal formulation of incidence and its order reversal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty subset \(F\subseteq C\), define \(N_C(F):=\bigcap_{x\in F}N_C(x)\). Then, for every \(u\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \[u\in N_C(F)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad F\subseteq F_C(u).\] Consequently, if \(F\subseteq G\subseteq C\), then \(N_C(G)\subseteq N_C(F)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A direction is normal along every point of a set exactly when its support face contains that set; face inclusion therefore reverses common-normal inclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u\in N_C(F)\iff F\subseteq F_C(u)\), and \(F\subseteq G\Rightarrow N_C(G)\subseteq N_C(F)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Face–Normal Antitonicity

children.title: Support Smoothness-Uniqueness Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Smoothness and strict-convexity correspondences expressed through support geometry.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Differentiability as Uniqueness of the Supporting Point
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex. Then \(\sigma_C\) is finite and convex on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(F_C(d)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in C}\langle x,d\rangle\) is nonempty for every \(d\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The correspondence is pointwise in direction and uses ordinary finite-dimensional Fréchet differentiability. The global strict-convexity equivalence is stated for compact convex sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The support smoothness-uniqueness correspondence is the identity
\[
\partial\sigma_C(d)=F_C(d)
=\{x\in C:\langle x,d\rangle=\sigma_C(d)\},
\qquad d\in\mathbb{R}^n.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\sigma_C\text{ is differentiable at }d
\iff F_C(d)\text{ is a singleton}.
\]
When \(F_C(d)=\{x_d\}\),
\[
\nabla\sigma_C(d)=x_d.
\]
Equivalently, the support value has a unique maximizing point exactly when the support function has a unique subgradient at that direction. Globally, \(C\) is strictly convex exactly when every nonzero supporting direction has a unique contact point, equivalently when \(\sigma_C\) is differentiable on \(\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The subdifferential of the support function at a direction is exactly the face exposed by that direction. Hence the support function is differentiable there precisely when the exposed face consists of one point, and its gradient is that unique support point. For a compact convex set, strict convexity is equivalent to this uniqueness, and therefore differentiability, in every nonzero direction.
assumptions_latex: Differentiability is considered at \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\); the strict-convexity equivalence uses \(d\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial\sigma_C(d)=F_C(d)\), so \(\sigma_C\) is differentiable at \(d\) iff \(F_C(d)=\{x_d\}\), in which case \(\nabla\sigma_C(d)=x_d\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(F_C(d)=\{x_d\}\iff \operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in C}\langle x,d\rangle=\{x_d\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A vector \(u\) has a unique support point on \(C\) when there is exactly one \(x_u\in C\) satisfying \[\langle u,x_u\rangle=h_C(u).\] Equivalently, \[F_C(u)=\{x_u\}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\partial h_C(u)=\{x_u\}.\] For \(u=0\), one has \(F_C(0)=C\), so uniqueness at the origin occurs only when \(C\) itself is a singleton. knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The support function is nondifferentiable at \(u\) exactly when its support face \(F_C(u)=\partial h_C(u)\) contains more than one point. Its one-sided directional derivative in any direction \(v\) exists and is represented by \[h_C'(u;v):=\lim_{t\downarrow0}\frac{h_C(u+tv)-h_C(u)}{t}=\max_{x\in F_C(u)}\langle v,x\rangle.\] Thus the local first-order nonsmoothness of \(h_C\) records the full geometry of the face exposed by \(u\), rather than a single supporting point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nondifferentiability occurs exactly at directions exposing multiple points, and directional derivatives are the support function of that exposed face.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mutually Inverse Set and Support Representations
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal C\) be the class of nonempty closed convex subsets of \(\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(\mathcal S\) be the class of proper closed sublinear functions \(p:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The representation is finite-dimensional and extended-valued. Properness excludes the identically infinite function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the support transform and supporting-set transform by
\[
\mathfrak S(C):=\sigma_C,
\qquad
\mathfrak C(p):=C_p:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle x,d\rangle\le p(d)\ \forall d\in\mathbb{R}^n\}.
\]
Support-function representation is the correspondence
\[
\mathfrak C(\mathfrak S(C))=C\quad(C\in\mathcal C),
\qquad
\mathfrak S(\mathfrak C(p))=p\quad(p\in\mathcal S).
\]
Thus \(C\mapsto\sigma_C\) is a bijection from \(\mathcal C\) onto \(\mathcal S\), with inverse \(p\mapsto C_p\). For an arbitrary nonempty set \(A\),
\[
\mathfrak C(\sigma_A)=\overline{\operatorname{co}}A,
\]
so complete support data represents exactly the closed convex hull of the original set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The support transform sends a nonempty closed convex set to its closed sublinear support function. The inverse transform takes all points whose linear values lie below the prescribed sublinear function in every direction. These transforms are mutually inverse on nonempty closed convex sets and proper closed sublinear functions. Applied to an arbitrary set, the inverse recovers its closed convex hull.
assumptions_latex: \(C\in\mathcal C\) or \(p\in\mathcal S\), according to the transform being used.
The fixed Euclidean pairing identifies points with continuous linear functionals.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(x\in C\iff \langle x,d\rangle\le\sigma_C(d)\ \forall d\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
\(p(d)=\sup\{\langle x,d\rangle:x\in C_p\}\).
special_cases_latex: A linear function \(p(d)=\langle x_0,d\rangle\) represents the singleton \(\{x_0\}\).
An everywhere-finite support function represents a bounded, hence compact, closed convex set.
immediate_consequences_latex: Two nonempty closed convex sets are equal iff their support functions agree in every direction.
Every proper closed sublinear function has at least one linear minorant.
boundary_notes: Without closedness and convexity, support data reconstructs only the closed convex hull.
A sublinear function that is not lower semicontinuous is not itself the support function of a set under this correspondence.
The representation permits \(+\infty\) values.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reconstruction from Complete Directional Support Data
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, with support function \(\sigma_C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The reconstruction uses all directions, although positive homogeneity permits restriction to a unit ball, unit sphere, or effective domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The reconstruction determined by a function \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is
\[
R(h):=\bigcap_{d\in\mathbb{R}^n}\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle x,d\rangle\le h(d)\}.
\]
For the support data of a nonempty closed convex set,
\[
R(\sigma_C)=C.
\]
Equivalently, for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\),
\[
x\in C
\iff \langle x,d\rangle\le\sigma_C(d)\quad\forall d\in\mathbb{R}^n.
\]
The quantifier may instead range over the Euclidean unit ball, the unit sphere, or \(\operatorname{dom}\sigma_C\). If \(A\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is merely nonempty, then
\[
R(\sigma_A)=\overline{\operatorname{co}}A.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reconstruction intersects, over all directions, the halfspaces whose thresholds are the supplied support values. For a nonempty closed convex set this returns exactly the original set. Membership is therefore equivalent to satisfying every support inequality. For arbitrary input sets, the same construction returns the closed convex hull.
assumptions_latex: Complete directional values \(\sigma_C(d)\) are available on a positively generating direction set.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(C=\{x:\langle x,d\rangle\le\sigma_C(d)\ \forall d\in B(0,1)\}\).
\(C=\{x:\langle x,d\rangle\le\sigma_C(d)\ \forall d\in\operatorname{dom}\sigma_C\}\).
special_cases_latex: If \(C\) is compact, it suffices to know \(\sigma_C\) on the unit sphere.
For \(C=\{x_0\}\), the inequalities reconstruct the unique point \(x_0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: \(\sigma_C=\sigma_D\Rightarrow C=D\) for nonempty closed convex \(C,D\).
Any point outside \(C\) violates at least one support inequality.
boundary_notes: A proper subset of directions reconstructs an outer approximation unless it is sufficient by positive homogeneity or other structure.
Closure and convexity are essential for exact recovery of the original set.
Numerically approximate support values generally produce an approximate outer description, not the exact equality stated here.

notation.meaning: intersection reconstruction induced by directional upper bounds h

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Supporting-half-space representation of closed convex sets and cones
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean half-space representation, including regularity, the whole-space convention, and the conic specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonempty closed convex set C\subset\mathbb{R}^n is the intersection of all its supporting half-spaces. More generally, C\subset\mathbb{R}^n is closed and convex if and only if it is an intersection of closed half-spaces, equivalently the solution set of a system of linear inequalities; such a set is regular at every point. The empty intersection is interpreted as \mathbb{R}^n. A set K\subset\mathbb{R}^n is a closed convex cone if and only if it is an intersection of closed half-spaces whose boundary hyperplanes contain 0; every supporting half-space of a closed convex cone has 0 on its boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty closed convex set is the intersection of its supporting half-spaces. Closed convex sets are exactly intersections of closed half-spaces, or solution sets of linear inequality systems, and they are regular everywhere. The empty intersection denotes the whole space. Closed convex cones are exactly intersections of closed half-spaces whose boundaries pass through the origin.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C\text{ is closed and convex}\iff C=\bigcap_{i\in I}H_i\text{ for closed half-spaces }H_i;\qquad K\text{ is a closed convex cone}\iff K=\bigcap_{i\in I}H_i\text{ with }0\in\partial H_i.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ordering and identification of closed convex sets by support functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inclusion and equality of nonempty closed convex sets inferred from their extended-valued support functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q_1,Q_2\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty closed convex sets and define
\[
\xi_{Q_i}(g):=\sup_{x\in Q_i}\langle g,x\rangle,\qquad i=1,2.
\]
If
\[
\xi_{Q_1}(g)\leq\xi_{Q_2}(g)\qquad\forall g\in\operatorname{dom}\xi_{Q_2},
\]
then \(Q_1\subseteq Q_2\). If, moreover,
\[
\operatorname{dom}\xi_{Q_1}=\operatorname{dom}\xi_{Q_2}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\xi_{Q_1}(g)=\xi_{Q_2}(g)\qquad\forall g\in\operatorname{dom}\xi_{Q_1},
\]
then \(Q_1=Q_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonempty closed convex sets, domination of one support function by another on the latter's effective domain implies set inclusion. Equality of the effective domains and all support values implies equality of the sets.
assumptions_latex: Q_1,Q_2\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\text{ are nonempty, closed, and convex}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reconstruction of a Closed Convex Set from Its Support Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between support-function generation and reconstruction by support halfspaces, with interchangeable direction sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(\sigma\) be a closed sublinear function. Then \[\sigma=\sigma_S\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad S=\{s\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle s,d\rangle\leq\sigma(d)\text{ for every }d\in X\},\] where \(X\) may be \(\mathbb{R}^n\), the closed unit ball, its boundary, or \(\operatorname{dom}\sigma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty closed convex set has support function sigma exactly when it is the intersection of the support halfspaces defined by sigma. The inequalities may be checked over all directions, the unit ball, the unit sphere, or the effective domain of sigma.

children.title: Support Order-Embedding Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Order correspondence between closed convex sets and support functions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal C\) be the partially ordered class of nonempty closed convex subsets of \(\mathbb{R}^n\), ordered by inclusion. Closed sublinear functions are ordered pointwise.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is an exact finite-dimensional order correspondence. Both directions require closed convex sets for the reverse implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The support map is an order embedding:
\[
C_1\subseteq C_2
\iff \sigma_{C_1}(d)\le\sigma_{C_2}(d)
\quad\forall d\in\mathbb{R}^n,
\qquad C_1,C_2\in\mathcal C.
\]
Accordingly, define
\[
C_1\preceq_{\sigma} C_2
\quad:\!\iff\quad
\sigma_{C_1}\le\sigma_{C_2}\text{ pointwise}.
\]
On \(\mathcal C\), this support order is exactly set inclusion. In particular,
\[
C_1=C_2\iff \sigma_{C_1}=\sigma_{C_2}.
\]
Because support functions are positively homogeneous, pointwise comparison may equivalently be checked on the unit sphere or unit ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One nonempty closed convex set is contained in another exactly when its support value is no larger in every direction. Thus the support-function map preserves and reflects order, and equality of support functions is equivalent to equality of the represented sets.
assumptions_latex: Function inequalities are interpreted pointwise in \(\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(C_1\subseteq C_2\iff \sigma_{C_1}|_{\mathbb S^{n-1}}\le\sigma_{C_2}|_{\mathbb S^{n-1}}\).
\(C_1=C_2\iff \sigma_{C_1}(d)=\sigma_{C_2}(d)\ \forall d\).
special_cases_latex: For singletons, \(\{x_1\}\subseteq\{x_2\}\iff\langle x_1,d\rangle\le\langle x_2,d\rangle\ \forall d\), which forces \(x_1=x_2\).
If \(C_2=C_1+rB\), then \(\sigma_{C_2}(d)=\sigma_{C_1}(d)+r\|d\|\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Support inequalities provide certificates for set inclusion.
A strict support inequality in one direction implies that the two represented sets are unequal.
boundary_notes: For arbitrary nonclosed or nonconvex sets, pointwise support order compares their closed convex hulls, not necessarily the original sets.
Pointwise strict inequality in every nonzero direction is stronger than strict set inclusion and is not equivalent to it.
Extended values must be retained for unbounded sets.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathcal{C}_n\), define the set-inclusion order by \[C\preceq_{\mathrm{set}}D\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad C\subseteq D.\] This is a partial order: it is reflexive, antisymmetric, and transitive. Its comparison is geometric and pointwise in membership: \(C\preceq_{\mathrm{set}}D\) means that every \(x\in C\) also belongs to \(D\). No boundedness assumption is imposed, so the associated support functions may be extended-real-valued.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonempty closed convex sets are partially ordered by ordinary set inclusion.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\sigma_C:E^*\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) by \(\sigma_C(u)=\sup_{c\in C}\langle u,c\rangle\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty closed convex set equals the intersection of all halfspaces whose bounds are supplied by its support function.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Canonical Outer Description by Supporting Halfspaces
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. For \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(H_C^-(d)=\{x:\langle x,d\rangle\le\sigma_C(d)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The representation is an exact, generally infinite outer description indexed by dual directions. Directions with infinite support impose no restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The supporting-halfspace representation of \(C\) is the family
\[
\mathcal H(C):=\{H_C^-(d):d\in\mathbb{R}^n\},
\qquad
H_C^-(d):=\{x:\langle x,d\rangle\le\sigma_C(d)\}.
\]
It satisfies
\[
C=\bigcap_{d\in\mathbb{R}^n}H_C^-(d).
\]
For each fixed \(d\in\operatorname{dom}\sigma_C\), the threshold \(\sigma_C(d)\) is minimal:
\[
\sigma_C(d)=\inf\{r\in\mathbb{R}:C\subseteq\{x:\langle x,d\rangle\le r\}\}.
\]
More generally, the halfspace \(H_{d,r}^-:=\{x:\langle x,d\rangle\le r\}\) contains \(C\) exactly when \(r\ge\sigma_C(d)\). Hence the canonical family keeps, for each normal direction, the tightest containing halfspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonempty closed convex set equals the intersection of its direction-indexed supporting halfspaces. In a fixed finite-support direction, the support value is the smallest halfspace threshold that still contains the set. Any larger threshold gives a redundant containing halfspace, while a smaller threshold cuts off part of the set.
assumptions_latex: \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\); minimal finite thresholds are considered only for \(d\in\operatorname{dom}\sigma_C\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(x\notin C\iff \exists d\text{ such that }\langle x,d\rangle>\sigma_C(d)\).
\(C=\bigcap_{(d,r)\in\operatorname{epi}\sigma_C}H_{d,r}^-\).
special_cases_latex: For a closed convex polyhedron, a finite subfamily may suffice, although the canonical family contains all valid directions.
If \(\sigma_C(d)=+\infty\), then the corresponding inequality is vacuous.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every exterior point is separated from \(C\) by at least one canonical support inequality.
Support data is an outer-description language for closed convex sets.
boundary_notes: The hyperplane boundary need not meet an unbounded set even when the support value is finite.
A finite sampled family generally yields only an outer approximation.
Exact equality may fail for a nonclosed or nonconvex original set; the intersection then gives its closed convex hull.

notation.meaning: closed halfspace with normal d and upper threshold r
canonical family of tight direction-indexed halfspaces

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lower-Semicontinuity Is the Exact Representation Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary for representing a proper sublinear function by its dominated linear functionals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p:E\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper and sublinear, and set
\[
C_p=\{u\in E^*: \langle u,x\rangle\leq p(x)\ \forall x\in E\}.
\]
Then \(\sigma_{C_p}=p^{**}=\operatorname{cl}p\leq p\); hence \(p=\sigma_{C_p}\) holds exactly when \(p\) is lower semicontinuous. Strict inequality can occur: for
\[
K=\{0\}\cup\{(s,t)\in\mathbb{R}^2:t>0\},\qquad p=\delta_K,
\]
\(p\) is proper sublinear but not lower semicontinuous, and \(\sigma_{C_p}=\delta_{\overline K}\neq p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without lower semicontinuity, dominated linear functionals represent only the closed hull of a sublinear function; the indicator of a nonclosed convex cone gives strict failure.

notation.meaning: Set of linear functionals dominated by p

knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Semicontinuity Is the Exact Representation Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset E^*\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. Its support function \(\sigma_C:E\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and sublinear, and
\[
C=\{u\in E^*: \langle u,x\rangle\leq\sigma_C(x)\ \text{for every }x\in E\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The support function of every nonempty closed convex dual set is a proper closed sublinear function, and its dominated-linear-functional set recovers the original set.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
\(C\subset E^*\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_C\) is proper lower-semicontinuous sublinear and \(C=\{u:\langle u,\cdot\rangle\leq\sigma_C\}\).

notation.meaning: Support function of the dual set

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Supporting Set of a Closed Sublinear Function
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(p:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, positively homogeneous, and subadditive.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The function may be extended-valued. Lower semicontinuity is essential for exact equality with a support function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The supporting set represented by \(p\) is
\[
C_p:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle x,d\rangle\le p(d)\ \forall d\in\mathbb{R}^n\}.
\]
It is a nonempty closed convex set, and \(p\) is its support function:
\[
p(d)=\sigma_{C_p}(d)=\sup_{x\in C_p}\langle x,d\rangle
\quad\forall d\in\mathbb{R}^n.
\]
Equivalently, \(p\) is the pointwise supremum of all linear functions that minorize it:
\[
p(d)=\sup\{\langle x,d\rangle:\langle x,u\rangle\le p(u)\ \forall u\in\mathbb{R}^n\}.
\]
The set \(C_p\) is uniquely determined among nonempty closed convex sets by this identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper closed sublinear function determines the set of all vectors whose associated linear functionals lie below it in every direction. This supporting set is nonempty, closed, and convex, and taking its support function recovers the original function. Thus every closed sublinear function is the supremum of its linear minorants and has a unique closed convex representing set.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is lower semicontinuous and sublinear on \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(C_p\) is the set of coefficients of all linear minorants of \(p\).
\(p=\sup_{x\in C_p}\langle x,\cdot\rangle\).
special_cases_latex: If \(p(d)=\langle x_0,d\rangle\), then \(C_p=\{x_0\}\).
If \(p\) is finite everywhere, then \(C_p\) is bounded and therefore compact.
immediate_consequences_latex: A proper closed sublinear function has at least one linear minorant.
The representing set is unique because closed convex sets are reconstructed from their support functions.
boundary_notes: If \(p\) is sublinear but not lower semicontinuous, the support of \(C_p\) represents its lower-semicontinuous hull rather than necessarily \(p\).
The representation is extended-valued and does not require boundedness of \(C_p\).
The identically infinite function is excluded because it is not proper.

notation.meaning: closed convex supporting set represented by p

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support-function representation of closed positively homogeneous convex functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes proper lower-semicontinuous convex positively homogeneous functions on a Hilbert space as support functions of nonempty closed convex sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\) be a Hilbert space, let \(f:\mathcal H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), and define \(C=\{u\in\mathcal H\mid (\forall x\in\mathcal H)\;\langle x,u\rangle\leq f(x)\}\). The following are equivalent: (i) \(f\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\) and \(f\) is positively homogeneous; (ii) \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex and \(f=\sigma_C\); (iii) \(f\) is the support function of a nonempty closed convex subset of \(\mathcal H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an extended-real-valued function f on a Hilbert space, form the set C of vectors whose linear functionals lie below f everywhere. Then f is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and positively homogeneous exactly when C is nonempty, closed, and convex and f is its support function; equivalently, f is the support function of some nonempty closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\) and \(f\) is positively homogeneous \(\Longleftrightarrow\) \(C\neq\varnothing\), \(C\) is closed and convex, and \(f=\sigma_C\) \(\Longleftrightarrow\) \(f\) is the support function of a nonempty closed convex subset of \(\mathcal H\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Representation of Closed Sublinear Functions by Linear Minorants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation of a closed sublinear function as the support function of its set of linear minorants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\sigma\) be a closed sublinear function on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), and define \[S_\sigma:=\{s\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle s,d\rangle\leq\sigma(d)\text{ for every }d\in\mathbb{R}^n\}.\] Then \(S_\sigma\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \[\sigma(d)=\sup_{s\in S_\sigma}\langle s,d\rangle\qquad(d\in\mathbb{R}^n).\] Equivalently, \(\sigma\) is the supremum of the linear functions minorizing it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every closed sublinear function has a linear minorant and is the pointwise supremum of all its linear minorants. Equivalently, it is the support function of the nonempty closed convex set of their coefficient vectors.
assumptions_latex: \(\sigma\) is a closed sublinear function on \(\mathbb{R}^n\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support-function representation of finite sublinear functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional conjugacy correspondence between nonempty compact convex sets and everywhere-finite sublinear functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fenchel conjugacy gives a bijection between nonempty compact convex sets \(C\subset\mathbf E\) and everywhere-finite sublinear functions on \(\mathbf E\). If \(C\) is nonempty, compact, and convex, then \(\delta_C^*\) is finite everywhere and sublinear. Conversely, if \(h:\mathbf E\to\mathbf R\) is sublinear, then \(h^*=\delta_C\), where \[C=\{\phi\in\mathbf E:\langle\phi,d\rangle\le h(d)\text{ for every }d\in\mathbf E\}\] is nonempty, compact, and convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The support function of a nonempty compact convex set is an everywhere-finite sublinear function. Conversely, every real-valued sublinear function is the support function of the nonempty compact convex set of vectors whose linear forms are dominated by it, and its conjugate is that set's indicator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support functions and closed sublinear representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the conjugacy correspondence between indicators of nonempty closed convex sets and proper closed positively homogeneous convex functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. Conversely, the conjugate of every proper closed positively homogeneous convex function is the indicator of a closed convex set.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: I_C^*=\sigma_C,\qquad \sigma_C(s)=\sup_{w\in C}w^\top s,\qquad f^*=I_{\{s:w^\top s\leq f(w)\ \forall w\}}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Infimal linear image as the support function of an adjoint preimage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear transformation of a support function into the representation of the set defined by an adjoint preimage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let A:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}^n be linear with adjoint A^*:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m. Let \varnothing\ne S\subset\mathbb{R}^m be closed and convex, let \sigma=\sigma_S, and define \[(A\sigma)(d):=\inf\{\sigma(p):Ap=d\}.\] If \sigma is minorized on A^{-1}(d) for every d\in\mathbb{R}^n, then \[\operatorname{cl}(A\sigma)=\sigma_{\{s\in\mathbb{R}^n:A^*s\in S\}}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the support function is bounded below on every fiber of A, the closure of its infimal linear image is the support function of the adjoint preimage of S.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed sublinear functions as support functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set–function representation with the empty-set exception and recession-domain polarity preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(D\subset\mathbb R^n\), \(\sigma_D\) is lsc and sublinear, and it is proper if \(D\neq\varnothing\), with \[\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{con}D)=\{v:\langle v,w\rangle\leq\sigma_D(w)\ \text{for all }w\}.\] Conversely, for a positively homogeneous function \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), let \[D_h:=\{v:\langle v,w\rangle\leq h(w)\ \text{for all }w\}.\] Then \(D_h\) is closed and convex. If \(D_h\neq\varnothing\), then \(\sigma_{D_h}=\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{con}h)\); if \(D_h=\varnothing\), then \(\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{con}h)\) is improper and has no finite values. Thus support functions give a bijection between nonempty closed convex subsets \(D\) of \(\mathbb R^n\) and proper lsc sublinear functions \(h\), with \[h=\sigma_D,\qquad D=\{v:\langle v,\cdot\rangle\leq h\}.\] Under this correspondence, \(D^\infty\) and \(\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{dom}h)\) are polar cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every support function is lower semicontinuous and sublinear and recovers the closed convex hull of its generating set. Conversely, a positively homogeneous function determines a closed convex set of dominated linear forms; when this set is nonempty, its support function is the closed convexification of the original function. This yields a bijection between nonempty closed convex sets and proper lower-semicontinuous sublinear functions, together with the stated recession-domain polarity.
assumptions_latex: h:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\text{ is positively homogeneous}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D\text{ nonempty, closed, convex}\ \longleftrightarrow\ h=\sigma_D\text{ proper, lsc, sublinear},\qquad D=\{v:\langle v,\cdot\rangle\leq h\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support Calculus for Standard Set Operations
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\{C_i\}_{i\in I}\) be nonempty subsets of finite-dimensional inner-product spaces, and let all support functions use the corresponding dual pairings.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The calculus is extended-valued. Closure and closed convex hull may appear because support functions retain only closed convex information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Support-function calculus is the collection of operation identities obtained by transporting set operations to support functions. Its canonical rules include
\[
\sigma_{\operatorname{cl}(\alpha C+\beta D)}=
\alpha\sigma_C+eta\sigma_D\qquad(\alpha,\beta>0),
\]
\[
\sigma_{\overline{\operatorname{co}}(\bigcup_{i\in I}C_i)}
=\sup_{i\in I}\sigma_{C_i},
\]
\[
\sigma_{\operatorname{cl}A(C)}(y)=\sigma_C(A^*y)
\]
for a linear map \(A\), and
\[
\sigma_{C\times D}(u,v)=\sigma_C(u)+\sigma_D(v).
\]
For nonempty intersections of closed convex sets, the corresponding rule is
\[
\sigma_{\bigcap_i C_i}=\overline{\operatorname{co}}\left(\inf_i\sigma_{C_i}\right),
\]
with pointwise infimum followed by the closed-convex hull as a function. These identities define the support calculus as an operation-preserving correspondence, with the stated closures accounting for possible nonclosed images or sums.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Support calculus translates weighted Minkowski sums into sums of support functions, closed convex hulls of unions into pointwise suprema, linear images into composition with the adjoint, and Cartesian products into separable sums. Intersections correspond to the closed convex hull of the pointwise infimum. Closure terms are retained whenever the underlying set operation need not preserve closedness.
assumptions_latex: Every set whose support is taken is nonempty.
For the intersection rule, the sets are closed and convex and their intersection is nonempty.
\(A^*\) denotes the adjoint relative to the chosen inner products.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Standard convex-set operations are transported to the displayed algebraic operations on support functions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\sigma_{\alpha C+\beta D}(d)=\alpha\sigma_C(d)+\beta\sigma_D(d)\) whenever the unclosed sum is used, since support is unchanged by closure.
\(\sigma_{\bigcup_i C_i}=\sup_i\sigma_{C_i}=\sigma_{\overline{\operatorname{co}}(\bigcup_i C_i)}\).
special_cases_latex: \(\sigma_{C+x_0}(d)=\sigma_C(d)+\langle x_0,d\rangle\).
\(\sigma_{-C}(d)=\sigma_C(-d)\).
\(\sigma_{rB}(d)=r\|d\|\) for \(r\ge0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Complicated set constructions can be compared through pointwise functional identities.
Closure of a set never changes its support function.
boundary_notes: The pointwise infimum of support functions need not itself be closed or convex, so the intersection rule requires regularization.
A linear image or Minkowski sum of closed convex sets need not be closed in every unbounded case.
The formulas do not encode nonconvex features lost under closed convexification.

children.title: Additive-Homogeneous Support Calculus
children.top_down_role: Support calculus for additive and homogeneous set operations.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C,D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, let \(a,b\ge0\), and define \(aC+bD:=\{ax+by:x\in C,\ y\in D\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The identities hold for arbitrary nonempty sets. A closure may be inserted on the set side without changing the support function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The additive-homogeneous support calculus is
\[
\sigma_{aC+bD}(d)=a\sigma_C(d)+b\sigma_D(d)
\quad\forall d\in\mathbb{R}^n,
\]
with the conventions \(0C:=\{0\}\) and \(0\cdot(+\infty):=0\). In particular,
\[
\sigma_{C+D}=\sigma_C+\sigma_D,
\qquad
\sigma_{aC}=a\sigma_C\quad(a\ge0).
\]
For any scalar \(t\in\mathbb{R}\), including negative values,
\[
\sigma_{tC}(d)=\sigma_C(td).
\]
Translations satisfy
\[
\sigma_{C+x_0}(d)=\sigma_C(d)+\langle x_0,d\rangle.
\]
If \(C,D\) are closed and convex, the function \(a\sigma_C+b\sigma_D\) represents \(\operatorname{cl}(aC+bD)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted Minkowski addition becomes pointwise weighted addition of support functions. Nonnegative set scaling becomes function scaling, arbitrary scalar multiplication can be transferred to the direction argument, and translation adds the corresponding linear functional. If a weighted sum of closed convex sets is not closed, its support function represents its closure.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\sigma_{\operatorname{cl}(aC+bD)}=a\sigma_C+b\sigma_D\).
\(\sigma_{-C}(d)=\sigma_C(-d)\).
special_cases_latex: For \(D=\{x_0\}\), Minkowski addition is translation.
For \(C=rB\), \(\sigma_C(d)=r\|d\|\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Minkowski sums can be reconstructed from sums of support functions after closed convexification.
Repeated Minkowski addition gives \(\sigma_{C_1+\cdots+C_m}=\sum_i\sigma_{C_i}\).
boundary_notes: When \(a=0\), defining \(0C=\{0\}\) avoids ambiguity for unbounded \(C\).
A sum of closed unbounded convex sets need not be closed.
Negative scaling is not represented by multiplying an extended-valued support function by a negative number; it acts on the direction instead.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support of a Union and Its Closed Convex Hull
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\{C_i\}_{i\in I}\) be a nonempty family of nonempty subsets of \(\mathbb{R}^n\), and set \(U:=\bigcup_{i\in I}C_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The index set may be infinite, and support values may be infinite. The result explicitly records the information loss caused by closed convexification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The union-hull support correspondence is
\[
\sigma_U(d)=\sup_{i\in I}\sigma_{C_i}(d)
\quad\forall d\in\mathbb{R}^n,
\]
and, because support is invariant under closure and convexification,
\[
\sigma_{\overline{\operatorname{co}}U}(d)
=\sigma_U(d)
=\sup_{i	ext{ in }I}\sigma_{C_i}(d).
\]
Hence the pointwise supremum of the family of support functions is the support function of the closed convex hull of the union:
\[
\sup_{i\in I}\sigma_{C_i}
=\sigma_{\overline{\operatorname{co}}(\bigcup_{i\in I}C_i)}.
\]
For two sets this becomes
\[
\sigma_{\overline{\operatorname{co}}(C\cup D)}=\max\{\sigma_C,\sigma_D\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The support value of a union is the supremum of the support values of its members. The union and its closed convex hull have identical support functions, so the pointwise supremum represents the closed convex hull of the union. For two sets, the operation is the pointwise maximum.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\sigma_{\bigcup_iC_i}=\sup_i\sigma_{C_i}\).
For finite \(I\), \(\sigma_{\operatorname{co}(\bigcup_iC_i)}=\max_i\sigma_{C_i}\), with closure harmless on the support side.
special_cases_latex: For points \(x_1,\ldots,x_m\), the support of their convex hull is \(d\mapsto\max_j\langle x_j,d\rangle\).
For two closed convex sets, the support of their closed convex hull is the pointwise maximum of their supports.
immediate_consequences_latex: Pointwise suprema of support functions are closed and sublinear when not identically infinite.
Convex-hull generation can be performed entirely in support-function coordinates.
boundary_notes: Support data cannot distinguish the union from its closed convex hull.
For an infinite family, the unclosed convex hull need not be closed.
The pointwise supremum may take \(+\infty\) even when every individual support value is finite at some directions.

notation.meaning: union of the indexed family of sets

children.title: Set-Union Support Values
children.top_down_role: Support values generated by aggregation through set union.

assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space with dual \(E^*\).
\(I\) is a nonempty index set, and \((C_i)_{i\in I}\) is a family of nonempty subsets of \(E\).

notation.meaning: Support function of the ith set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arbitrary nonempty families of nonempty sets.

source_refs.locator: 1.3 Convex Combinations and Convex Hulls p. 94

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(u\in E^*\), taking the supremum over a union is equivalent to taking the supremum of the member support values: \[\sigma_{\bigcup_{i\in I}C_i}(u)=\sup_{c\in\bigcup_{i\in I}C_i}\langle u,c\rangle=\sup_{i\in I}\sigma_{C_i}(u).\] The equality is interpreted in \(\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The support value of a union is the supremum of the support values of its member sets.
knowledge_statements.title: Set-Union Support Values

source_witnesses.locator: 1.3 Convex Combinations and Convex Hulls p. 94
source_witnesses.source_title: Convex Analysis and Minimization Algorithms I: Fundamentals

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact attainment structure behind the supremum of member support values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=\bigcup_{i\in I}C_i\), \(M(u)=\sup_{j\in I}\sigma_{C_j}(u)\), and \(I(u)=\{i:\sigma_{C_i}(u)=M(u)\}\). Then \[F_U(u)=\bigcup_{i\in I(u)}F_{C_i}(u).\] Thus union support is attained exactly when some member attains both the outer family supremum and its own support value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A union maximizer is exactly a maximizer from a member having maximal support among the family.

notation.meaning: Points of S attaining support in direction u.
Indices attaining the family support supremum.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support Functions Are Invariant under Closure and Convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-value invariance for arbitrary nonempty Euclidean sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every nonempty set \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\),
\[\sigma_S=\sigma_{\operatorname{cl}S}=\sigma_{\operatorname{co}S}=\sigma_{\overline{\operatorname{co}}S}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closing or convexifying a nonempty set, separately or together, does not change its support function.

children.title: Union–Hull Indistinguishability
children.top_down_role: Support-level information shared by a union plus its convex hull.

assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space with dual \(E^*\).
\(I\) is a nonempty index set, and \((C_i)_{i\in I}\) is a family of nonempty subsets of \(E\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support functions cannot distinguish a union from its convex hull.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=\bigcup_{i\in I}C_i\). For every \(u\in E^*\), \[\sigma_U(u)=\sup_{i\in I}\sigma_{C_i}(u)=\sigma_{\operatorname{conv}U}(u).\] Hence the union and its convex hull have identical support functions, even when the union is nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A union and its convex hull have the same support function, so support data cannot distinguish them.

children.title: Infinite-Family Hull Regimes
children.top_down_role: Closure-sensitive support behavior for hulls generated by infinite families.

notation.meaning: Support function of the ith set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arbitrary families with closed convexification in finite dimensions.

source_refs.locator: 1.3 Convex Combinations and Convex Hulls p. 94
source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Minimization Algorithms I: Fundamentals

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an arbitrary nonempty index set \(I\), put \(U=\bigcup_{i\in I}C_i\). Continuity of each linear functional and invariance under convexification yield, for every \(u\in E^*\), \[\sigma_{\overline{\operatorname{conv}}U}(u)=\sigma_U(u)=\sup_{i\in I}\sigma_{C_i}(u).\] No compactness, boundedness, or finiteness of the family is required; the common value may be \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For any family, the closed convex hull of its union has support equal to the pointwise supremum of member supports.
knowledge_statements.title: Infinite-Family Hull Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: 1.3 Convex Combinations and Convex Hulls p. 94
source_witnesses.source_title: Convex Analysis and Minimization Algorithms I: Fundamentals

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closure Restores an Unattained Infinite-Family Support Value
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical distinction between an infinite union’s algebraic and closed convex hulls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\geq1\), let \(C_n=\{1-1/n\}\subset\mathbb R\) and \(U=\bigcup_{n\geq1}C_n\). Then \(\operatorname{conv}U=[0,1)\), \(\overline{\operatorname{conv}}U=[0,1]\), and in direction \(1\), \[\sup_n\sigma_{C_n}(1)=\sigma_U(1)=\sigma_{\operatorname{conv}U}(1)=\sigma_{\overline{\operatorname{conv}}U}(1)=1.\] Only the closed convex hull attains the value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A countable family has support value one, but its union and ordinary convex hull do not attain it; closing the hull adds the maximizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All four support values equal \(1\), but only \(\overline{\operatorname{conv}}U\) attains it.
knowledge_statements.title: Closure Restores an Unattained Infinite-Family Support Value

children.title: Linear-Adjoint Support Transport
children.top_down_role: Support transformations induced by linear mappings.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Transport of Support Through a Linear Image
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(E\) and \(F\) be finite-dimensional inner-product spaces, let \(A:E\to F\) be linear with adjoint \(A^*:F\to E\), and let \(C\subset E\) be nonempty.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: No convexity or boundedness is needed. Closure may be placed on the image because support functions are closure-invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The linear-adjoint support transport of \(C\) through \(A\) is the identity
\[
\sigma_{A(C)}(y)=\sigma_C(A^*y)
\quad\forall y\in F.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\sigma_{\operatorname{cl}A(C)}=\sigma_C\circ A^*.
\]
Thus a direction \(y\) in the image space is pulled back to the direction \(A^*y\) in the source space. The effective domain transforms as
\[
\operatorname{dom}\sigma_{A(C)}
=\{y\in F:A^*y\in\operatorname{dom}\sigma_C\}
=(A^*)^{-1}(\operatorname{dom}\sigma_C).
\]
For an affine image \(A(C)+b\),
\[
\sigma_{A(C)+b}(y)=\sigma_C(A^*y)+\langle b,y\rangle_F.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The support of a linear image in an image-space direction equals the original support in the adjoint-pulled-back direction. Consequently, the finite-support domain is the inverse image under the adjoint of the original finite-support domain. Adding a translation contributes the corresponding linear functional.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\sigma_{\operatorname{cl}A(C)}=\sigma_C\circ A^*\).
\(y\in\operatorname{dom}\sigma_{A(C)}\iff A^*y\in\operatorname{dom}\sigma_C\).
special_cases_latex: For \(A=tI\), \(\sigma_{tC}(d)=\sigma_C(td)\).
For an orthogonal map \(Q\), \(\sigma_{Q C}(y)=\sigma_C(Q^{-1}y)\).
For a coordinate projection, support is obtained by evaluating the original support on directions with zero discarded component.
immediate_consequences_latex: Linear-image support computations require no explicit image-set construction.
If \(C\) is compact, then \(A(C)\) is compact and its support is finite everywhere.
boundary_notes: A linear image of a closed convex unbounded set need not be closed, hence the explicit closure in the representation form.
The formula uses the adjoint determined by the selected inner products.
This rule concerns direct images; inverse images require different qualification conditions.

notation.meaning: adjoint of A under the chosen inner products

children.title: Linear-Image Support Transport
children.top_down_role: Support representation of sets transported into a codomain.

assumptions_latex: \(A:E\to F\) is linear between finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact support transport through a finite-dimensional linear image.

source_refs.locator: 2.1 Image of a Function Under a Linear Mapping p. 54
source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Minimization Algorithms II: Advanced Theory and Bundle Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A^*:F^*\to E^*\) be determined by \(\langle A^*v,x\rangle=\langle v,Ax\rangle\). Then every \(v\in F^*\) satisfies \[\sigma_{A(C)}(v)=\sup_{c\in C}\langle v,Ac\rangle=\sup_{c\in C}\langle A^*v,c\rangle=\sigma_C(A^*v).\] Thus a dual direction is transported backward through the adjoint before evaluating the original support function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The support of a linear image at a dual direction equals the original support evaluated at the adjoint direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Image Support Transport

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1 Image of a Function Under a Linear Mapping p. 54
source_witnesses.source_title: Convex Analysis and Minimization Algorithms II: Advanced Theory and Bundle Methods

children.title: Linear-Preimage Support Transport
children.top_down_role: Support representation of inverse-image sets under linear mappings.

assumptions_latex: \(A:E\to F\) is linear between finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
\(C\subset F\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_{A^{-1}(C)}(u)=\min\{\sigma_C(v):v\in F^*,\ A^*v=u\}\) for every \(u\in E^*\), with \(\min\varnothing:=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional preimage formula under a relative-interior qualification.

source_refs.locator: 2.1 Image of a Function Under a Linear Mapping p. 54
source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Minimization Algorithms II: Advanced Theory and Bundle Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the relative-interior qualification, the preimage is nonempty and its support is obtained by minimizing over dual lifts. For every \(u\in E^*\), \[\sigma_{A^{-1}(C)}(u)=\min\{\sigma_C(v):v\in F^*,\ A^*v=u\},\] where the minimum over an empty feasible set is \(+\infty\). When a lift exists, the minimum is attained; directions outside \(\operatorname{range}A^*\) therefore have support value \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a relative-interior qualification, preimage support is the minimum support of the target set over all adjoint lifts of the direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Preimage Support Transport

children.title: Adjoint Direction Transport
children.top_down_role: Movement of supporting directions through the adjoint mapping.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq X\) is nonempty and \(L:X\to Y\) is linear.

notation.meaning: Support function of a nonempty set S.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact support transport for a linear image in finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces.

source_refs.locator: 7.2 Support Functions p. 135
source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Monotone Operator Theory in Hilbert Spaces

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(y\in Y\), linear-image support is transported to the adjoint direction: \[\sigma_{L(C)}(y)=\sup_{x\in C}\langle y,Lx\rangle=\sup_{x\in C}\langle L^*y,x\rangle=\sigma_C(L^*y).\] This identity remains valid with values in \(\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\); neither convexity nor closedness of \(C\) is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The support of a linear image in direction y equals the original set's support in the adjoint direction L*y.
knowledge_statements.title: Adjoint Direction Transport

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 Support Functions p. 135

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Transport of Support Points and Exposed Faces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise realization of adjoint direction transport for support maximizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(u\in X\), define
\[
F_C(u):=\{x\in C:\langle u,x\rangle=\sigma_C(u)\},
\]
with this set empty when the support supremum is not attained. Then every \(y\in Y\) satisfies
\[
F_{L(C)}(y)=L\bigl(F_C(L^*y)\bigr).
\]
Equivalently, \(Lx\) is a support point of \(L(C)\) in direction \(y\) exactly when \(x\) is a support point of \(C\) in direction \(L^*y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Support maximizers of a linear image are precisely the images of support maximizers in the adjoint-transformed direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Transport of Support Points and Exposed Faces

children.title: Rank-Deficient Mapping Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Domain, kernel, plus range effects in support transformations.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces, and \(L:X\to Y\) is linear.

notation.meaning: Inverse image of D under L.
Adjoint of L and its range.
Support function of a nonempty subset S of X.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kernel directions delimit finite support of a nonempty linear preimage.

source_refs.locator: 2.2 Pre-Composition with an Affine Mapping p. 56
source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Minimization Algorithms II: Advanced Theory and Bundle Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(u\in X\), if \(u\notin\operatorname{ran}L^*=(\ker L)^\perp\), then \[\sigma_{L^{-1}(D)}(u)=+\infty.\] Thus membership in \(\operatorname{ran}L^*\) is necessary, but not sufficient by itself, for finite support of the nonempty preimage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty linear preimage has infinite support in every direction outside the range of the adjoint; belonging to that range is necessary but not sufficient for finite support.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficient Mapping Boundaries

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Kernel Invariance of a Linear Preimage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric source of the rank-deficient support boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=L^{-1}(D)\neq\varnothing\). Then \(C+k=C\) for every \(k\in\ker L\). If \(D\) is convex, then \(C\) is convex and \(\ker L\subseteq\operatorname{lin}C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear preimage is invariant under kernel translations; for a convex target, the kernel is contained in its lineality space.
assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces and \(L:X\to Y\) is linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L^{-1}(D)+\ker L=L^{-1}(D)\), and if \(D\) is convex then \(\ker L\subseteq\operatorname{lin}(L^{-1}(D))\).

notation.meaning: Lineality space of the convex set C.

children.title: Product-Space Support Calculus
children.top_down_role: Support calculus in product and projected spaces.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(E,F\) be finite-dimensional inner-product spaces. Equip \(E\times F\) with \(\langle(x,y),(u,v)\rangle=\langle x,u\rangle_E+\langle y,v\rangle_F\). Let \(C\subset E\) and \(D\subset F\) be nonempty.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The product rule is extended-valued and requires no convexity. The projection rule applies to any nonempty subset of a product space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The support function of a Cartesian product separates by coordinates:
\[
\sigma_{C\times D}(u,v)=\sigma_C(u)+\sigma_D(v)
\quad\forall(u,v)\in E\times F.
\]
If \(S\subset E\times F\) is nonempty and \(P_E(x,y)=x\), then
\[
\sigma_{P_E(S)}(u)=\sigma_S(u,0)
\quad\forall u\in E.
\]
More generally, for an orthogonal projection \(P_V:E\to V\) onto a subspace \(V\),
\[
\sigma_{P_V(C)}(v)=\sigma_C(v)
\quad\forall v\in V.
\]
Closures may be added to the projected sets without changing these functions. These identities define product-space support calculus by separating independent product coordinates and embedding projected directions with zeros in the eliminated coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The support of a Cartesian product is the sum of the component support functions. The support of a projection is obtained by evaluating the original support function at a direction whose discarded coordinates are zero. For an orthogonal projection onto a subspace, the projected support is simply the restriction of the original support to that subspace.
assumptions_latex: \(C,D,S\) are nonempty in their stated spaces.
Product pairings are the sums of the component inner products.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\sigma_{\operatorname{cl}P_E(S)}(u)=\sigma_S(u,0)\).
\(\operatorname{dom}\sigma_{C\times D}=\operatorname{dom}\sigma_C\times\operatorname{dom}\sigma_D\).
special_cases_latex: For \(D=\{0\}\), \(\sigma_{C\times\{0\}}(u,v)=\sigma_C(u)\).
For \(S=C\times D\), projection onto \(E\) recovers \(C\) and restriction at \((u,0)\) recovers \(\sigma_C(u)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Support computations for rectangular uncertainty sets decompose componentwise.
Projection can be analyzed without explicitly eliminating the discarded variables.
boundary_notes: Projection must not be confused with the slice \(\{x:(x,0)\in S\}\); the latter has a different support rule.
A projection of a closed convex set need not be closed in an unbounded setting.
The sum uses extended-real arithmetic, so it may equal \(+\infty\).

notation.meaning: coordinate projection from E times F onto E
dual direction u embedded with zero discarded component

children.title: Product-Set Support Calculus
children.top_down_role: Support structure of Cartesian products across component spaces.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable support calculus for Cartesian products.

source_refs.locator: 7.2 Support Functions p. 135
source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Monotone Operator Theory in Hilbert Spaces

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \((u,v)\in X\times Y\), the independent suprema separate: \[\sigma_{A\times B}(u,v)=\sup_{x\in A,\,y\in B}\bigl(\langle u,x\rangle+\langle v,y\rangle\bigr)=\sigma_A(u)+\sigma_B(v).\] The equality is interpreted in \(\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), where the sum is always well-defined because support functions of nonempty sets never take the value \(-\infty\). Convexity and closedness are unnecessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The support function of a Cartesian product is the sum of the support functions of its factors.
knowledge_statements.title: Product-Set Support Calculus

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 Support Functions p. 135
source_witnesses.source_title: Convex Analysis and Monotone Operator Theory in Hilbert Spaces

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exposed Faces of a Cartesian Product
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimizer structure accompanying separable product support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(F_S(w)=\{s\in S:\langle w,s\rangle=\sigma_S(w)\}\). Then \[F_{A\times B}(u,v)=F_A(u)\times F_B(v).\] Thus product support is attained exactly when both factor support values are attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The support maximizers of a Cartesian product are exactly the products of the factor maximizers.

notation.meaning: Points of S attaining its support value in direction w.

knowledge_statements.title: Exposed Faces of a Cartesian Product

children.title: Slice Support Geometry
children.top_down_role: Support behavior for affine or coordinate sections.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support of a nonempty fiber obtained by fixing one product coordinate.

source_refs.locator: 7.2 Support Functions p. 135
source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Monotone Operator Theory in Hilbert Spaces

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(u\in X\), fixing the second coordinate gives \[\sigma_{C_{y_0}}(u)=\sup\{\langle u,x\rangle:(x,y_0)\in C\}.\] The value lies in \(\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) and need not be attained when the slice is noncompact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A slice's support is the supremum of the first-coordinate linear functional over points of the original set having the prescribed second coordinate; the value may be infinite or unattained.
knowledge_statements.title: Slice Support Geometry

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 Support Functions p. 135
source_witnesses.source_title: Convex Analysis and Monotone Operator Theory in Hilbert Spaces

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Recession Geometry of a Coordinate Slice
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-convex slice geometry and its boundedness boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(C\) is closed and convex and \(C_{y_0}\neq\varnothing\), then \(C_{y_0}\) is closed and convex and \[\operatorname{rec}C_{y_0}=\{d\in X:(d,0_Y)\in\operatorname{rec}C\}.\] Consequently, \(C_{y_0}\) is bounded exactly when this set equals \(\{0_X\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The recession directions of a closed convex slice are exactly the horizontal recession directions of the original set.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq X\times Y\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rec}C_{y_0}=\{d:(d,0_Y)\in\operatorname{rec}C\}\), and \(C_{y_0}\) is bounded iff this cone is \(\{0_X\}\).

notation.meaning: Coordinate slice of C at y0.

knowledge_statements.title: Recession Geometry of a Coordinate Slice

children.title: Projected-Set Support Calculus

children.title: Marginalization Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Attainment plus closure issues arising from slices or projections.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary feasibility can preserve the dual value without producing a finite multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:y\geq x^2\}\), \(y_0=0\), and \(u\neq0\). Then \(C_0=\{0\}\), \(\sigma_{C_0}(u)=0\), and \[\sigma_C(u,v)=\begin{cases}-u^2/(4v),&v<0,\\+\infty,&v\geq0.\end{cases}\] Consequently \(\inf_v\sigma_C(u,v)=0\), but the infimum is not attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the zero-height slice of the squared epigraph, marginal duality has the correct value but no minimizing multiplier.

notation.meaning: Boundary slice of C at height zero.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Qualified Marginal Duality for Slice Support
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact multiplier representation under relative-interior feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(u\in X\), weak duality gives \[\sigma_{C_{y_0}}(u)\leq\inf_{v\in Y}\{\sigma_C(u,v)-\langle v,y_0\rangle\}.\] If \(y_0\in\operatorname{ri}P_Y(C)\), then the infimum is attained and \[\sigma_{C_{y_0}}(u)=\min_{v\in Y}\{\sigma_C(u,v)-\langle v,y_0\rangle\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Marginal dualization always upper-bounds slice support, and relative-interior feasibility makes the multiplier formula exact and attained.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq X\times Y\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Weak duality always holds; if \(y_0\in\operatorname{ri}P_Y(C)\), equality holds with a minimizing multiplier.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closure Form of Unqualified Marginal Duality

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(q(u)=\inf_{v\in Y}\{\sigma_C(u,v)-\langle v,y_0\rangle\}\). Without a qualification, \[\sigma_{C_{y_0}}=\operatorname{cl}q,\] where \(\operatorname{cl}q\) is the lower-semicontinuous convex hull of \(q\). Hence equality at \(u\) requires no closure correction there; attainment of the infimum is a separate issue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without qualification, slice support is the lower-semicontinuous closure of the multiplier infimum; value exactness and multiplier attainment are distinct questions.
