children.title: Signed Atomic Sets
children.top_down_role: Atomic constructions permitting positive or negative coefficients.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite real dictionaries closed under sign reversal.

source_refs.locator: 3 Convex Sets p. 49
source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Monotone Operator Theory in Hilbert Spaces

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The signed enlargement of \(\mathcal A_0\) is \(\mathcal A_\pm=\mathcal A_0\cup(-\mathcal A_0)\). With \(A=[a_1\ \cdots\ a_m]\), its convex hull satisfies \[\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A_\pm)=\{Ac:c\in\mathbb R^m,\ \|c\|_1\leq1\}.\] Consequently, its gauge has the coefficient representation \[\gamma_{\mathcal A_\pm}(x)=\inf\{\|c\|_1:Ac=x\},\] where the value is \(+\infty\) if \(x\notin\operatorname{span}(\mathcal A_0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding each atom’s negative converts nonnegative atomic mass into signed coefficients, and the resulting gauge is minimum coefficient ℓ1 mass.
knowledge_statements.title: Signed Atomic Sets

source_witnesses.locator: 3 Convex Sets p. 49
source_witnesses.source_title: Convex Analysis and Monotone Operator Theory in Hilbert Spaces

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Norm and Degeneracy Boundary for Signed Atomic Gauges
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definiteness and domain of a finite signed atomic gauge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C=\operatorname{conv}\{\pm a_1,\ldots,\pm a_m\}\), the gauge \(\gamma_C\) is even and is a norm on \(L=\operatorname{span}\{a_i\}\). On \(\mathbb R^d\), it is an everywhere-finite norm exactly when \(L=\mathbb R^d\); otherwise \(\gamma_C(x)=+\infty\) for \(x\notin L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite signed dictionary defines a norm on its span and an ambient-space norm exactly when its atoms span the ambient space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_C\) is a norm on \(L=\operatorname{span}\{a_i\}\), and it is a norm on \(\mathbb R^d\iff L=\mathbb R^d\).
knowledge_statements.title: Norm and Degeneracy Boundary for Signed Atomic Gauges

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polar and Dual Formula for a Signed Dictionary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite signed dictionaries in a real Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\operatorname{conv}\{\pm a_1,\ldots,\pm a_m\}\) and \(A=[a_1\ \cdots\ a_m]\). Then \[C^\circ=\{y\in\mathbb R^d:\|A^\top y\|_\infty\leq1\}\] and \[\gamma_C(x)=\sup\{\langle x,y\rangle:\|A^\top y\|_\infty\leq1\}.\] For \(x\in\operatorname{span}\{a_i\}\), the supremum is attained and equals the minimum coefficient \(\ell_1\)-mass in the seed representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polar is defined by absolute atom inequalities, and the signed atomic gauge is their dual support maximum.

notation.meaning: polar of the signed atomic hull

knowledge_statements.title: Polar and Dual Formula for a Signed Dictionary

children.title: Conic Atomic Sets
children.top_down_role: Atomic constructions governed by nonnegative conic combinations.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subset X\) is a nonempty cone, so \(\lambda K\subseteq K\) for every \(\lambda\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degeneracy caused by using an entire cone, rather than a bounded conic base, as the gauge unit set.

source_refs.locator: 6.3 Polar and Dual Cones p. 122
source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Monotone Operator Theory in Hilbert Spaces

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the atomic unit set is itself a cone \(K\), then \(tK=K\) for every \(t>0\). Hence its Minkowski functional collapses to \[\gamma_K(x)=\inf\{t>0:x\in tK\}=\begin{cases}0,&x\in K,\\+\infty,&x\notin K.\end{cases}\] Thus a nontrivial conic atomic model requires a normalized base or cross-section of the cone as its unit atoms; using the whole cone cannot produce a definite gauge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Using an entire cone as the atomic unit set makes the gauge zero on the cone and infinite outside; a normalized conic base is required.
knowledge_statements.title: Conic Atomic Sets

source_witnesses.locator: 6.3 Polar and Dual Cones p. 122
source_witnesses.source_title: Convex Analysis and Monotone Operator Theory in Hilbert Spaces

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalization of a cone by a strictly positive linear functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subset X\) be a convex cone and let \(u\in X^*\) satisfy \(\langle u,k\rangle>0\) for every \(k\in K\setminus\{0\}\). Define \[B=\{k\in K:\langle u,k\rangle=1\},\qquad C=\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup B).\] Every \(x\in K\setminus\{0\}\) has the representation \[x=\langle u,x\rangle b,\qquad b=\frac{x}{\langle u,x\rangle}\in B,\] and \[\gamma_C(x)=\begin{cases}\langle u,x\rangle,&x\in K,\\+\infty,&x\notin K.\end{cases}\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly positive linear normalization cuts a cone into a base whose gauge equals the normalization value on the cone and is infinite outside it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The gauge of \(\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup B)\) equals \(\langle u,x\rangle\) on \(K\) and \(+\infty\) outside \(K\).
review_flags: Existence of a strictly positive normalizing functional is assumed, not asserted for every cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Conic Base Gauge

children.title: Coefficient-Symmetry Regimes
children.top_down_role: Geometric distinctions produced by symmetry and coefficient-sign choices.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of one-sided and sign-symmetric finite-dictionary coefficient models.

source_refs.locator: 3.4 Polyhedral Functions p. 76
source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Minimization Algorithms II: Advanced Theory and Bundle Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the one-sided hull \(C_+=\operatorname{conv}(\{0,a_1,\ldots,a_m\})\), coefficients are constrained by sign and \[\gamma_+(x)=\inf\{\mathbf1^\top\lambda:A\lambda=x,\ \lambda\geq0\}.\] For the sign-symmetric hull \(C_\pm=\operatorname{conv}\{\pm a_1,\ldots,\pm a_m\}\), coefficient signs are free and \[\gamma_\pm(x)=\inf\{\|c\|_1:Ac=x\}.\] Equivalently, \(\gamma_\pm(x)=\inf_{x=u-v}\bigl(\gamma_+(u)+\gamma_+(v)\bigr)\), with extended-value conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One-sided atoms require nonnegative coefficients and total mass, while sign-symmetric atoms permit signed coefficients and charge their ℓ1 mass.
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient-Symmetry Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4 Polyhedral Functions p. 76
source_witnesses.source_title: Convex Analysis and Minimization Algorithms II: Advanced Theory and Bundle Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Constraints in One-Sided and Sign-Symmetric Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dictionary comparison of polar unit balls for the two coefficient regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=[a_1\ \cdots\ a_m]\), \[C_+=\operatorname{conv}(\{0,a_1,\ldots,a_m\}),\qquad C_\pm=\operatorname{conv}\{\pm a_1,\ldots,\pm a_m\}.\] Then \[C_+^\circ=\{z:A^\top z\le\mathbf1\},\qquad C_\pm^\circ=\{z:\|A^\top z\|_\infty\le1\}.\] Equivalently, \[\gamma_{C_+}^{\circ}(z)=\max\{0,\max_i\langle z,a_i\rangle\},\qquad \gamma_{C_\pm}^{\circ}(z)=\max_i|\langle z,a_i\rangle|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One-sided coefficients produce one-sided dual inequalities, whereas signed coefficients produce absolute dual inequalities and an infinity-norm polar value.
assumptions_latex: \(C_+\) and \(C_\pm\) are the one-sided and sign-symmetric atomic hulls.

notation.meaning: One-sided and sign-symmetric atomic unit sets.

children.title: Atomic Decompositions
children.top_down_role: Decomposition interfaces between atoms and gauge values.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polar Certificate for an Optimal Atomic Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-duality lower bounds and equality certificates for atomic coefficient mass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup\mathcal A)\). If \(x=\sum_i c_i a_i\), where \(c_i\ge0\) and \(a_i\in\mathcal A\), and \(z\) satisfies \(\sup_{a\in\mathcal A}\langle z,a\rangle\le1\), then \[\langle z,x\rangle\le\gamma_C(x)\le\sum_i c_i.\] Hence the decomposition is gauge-optimal whenever \(\langle z,x\rangle=\sum_i c_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polar-feasible vector lower-bounds atomic mass; equality with the mass of a feasible decomposition certifies optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(x=\sum_i c_i a_i\) is a finite nonnegative atomic decomposition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle z,x\rangle\le\gamma_C(x)\le\sum_i c_i\), with equality certifying optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Polar Certificate for an Optimal Atomic Decomposition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Attainment of Atomic Mass over Compact Dictionaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional compact atomic sets; extended-valued gauges are allowed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) have dimension \(d<\infty\), let \(\mathcal A\subset X\) be nonempty and compact, and set \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup\mathcal A)\). If \(\gamma_C(x)<+\infty\), then there are \(r\le d+1\), atoms \(a_j\in\mathcal A\), and coefficients \(c_j\ge0\) such that \[x=\sum_{j=1}^r c_j a_j,\qquad \gamma_C(x)=\sum_{j=1}^r c_j.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a compact finite-dimensional dictionary, every finite atomic-gauge value has an attaining decomposition using at most d+1 atoms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimal decomposition exists and can use at most \(d+1\) atoms.

notation.meaning: Gauge of the atomic unit set.

knowledge_statements.title: Attainment of Atomic Mass over Compact Dictionaries

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Carathéodory Support Bound for Atomic Decompositions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional sparsification of feasible decompositions; no attainment claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\dim X=d<\infty\) and suppose \[x=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i a_i,\qquad c_i\ge0,\quad a_i\in\mathcal A.\] There exist \(r\le d+1\), atoms \(b_j\in\mathcal A\), and \(\lambda_j\ge0\) such that \[x=\sum_{j=1}^r\lambda_j b_j,\qquad \sum_{j=1}^r\lambda_j=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i.\] Thus restricting to at most \(d+1\) atoms does not change the atomic-mass infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every feasible finite-dimensional atomic decomposition can be replaced by one using at most d+1 atoms with the same mass.
assumptions_latex: A finite nonnegative atomic decomposition of \(x\) is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A decomposition with at most \(d+1\) atoms and the same total mass exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Carathéodory Support Bound for Atomic Decompositions

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a real vector space of dimension \(d<\infty\).
\(\mathcal A\subset X\) is nonempty and \(0\in\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)=\inf\{\sum_{i=1}^{m}c_i:x=\sum_{i=1}^{m}c_i a_i,\ c_i\ge0,\ a_i\in\mathcal A,\ m\in\mathbb N\}\).

notation.meaning: Atomic set and its convex hull.
Gauge of the convex atomic hull.

standard_field_rationale: standard conic decomposition formula for the Minkowski functional of an atomic convex hull.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional nonnegative atomic decompositions; attainment of the infimum is not asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\) and \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)=\inf\{t\ge0:x\in tC\}\), with \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). Then
\[
\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)=\inf\left\{\sum_{i=1}^{m}c_i:
 x=\sum_{i=1}^{m}c_i a_i,\ c_i\ge0,\ a_i\in\mathcal A,\ m\in\mathbb N\right\}.
\]
Thus every feasible atomic decomposition supplies an upper bound on the gauge, while the gauge is the infimum of the total nonnegative coefficient mass over all such decompositions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The atomic gauge equals the least total nonnegative coefficient mass among all finite representations of a vector by atoms.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be finite-dimensional, let \(\mathcal A\subseteq X\), and let \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}\) be the gauge of \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A\cup\{0\})\). Fix \(x\in\operatorname{dom}\gamma_{\mathcal A}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite atomic sums in a finite-dimensional space; both exact minimizing decompositions and nonattained infima are covered.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An atomic decomposition of \(x\) is a finite family \((c_i,a_i)_{i=1}^m\) satisfying \(c_i\ge0\), \(a_i\in\mathcal A\), and \(x=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i a_i\). Its cost is \(\sum_i c_i\). It is gauge-attaining when \[\sum_{i=1}^m c_i=\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x).\] For \(\varepsilon\ge0\), it is an \(\varepsilon\)-atomic decomposition when \[\sum_{i=1}^m c_i\le\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)+\varepsilon.\] In the symmetric regime, the same object may be written \(x=\sum_i\alpha_i a_i\) with cost \(\sum_i|\alpha_i|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An atomic decomposition represents a point as a finite nonnegative combination of atoms and measures its quality by total coefficient weight. A decomposition is exact for the gauge when that weight equals the atomic gauge value. Approximate decompositions allow an additive tolerance. For a symmetric atom set, signed coefficients and their absolute-value sum give the equivalent representation.
assumptions_latex: Each decomposition uses finitely many atoms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The decomposition cost upper-bounds \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)\), with equality precisely for a gauge-attaining decomposition.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(x\ne0\), a gauge-attaining decomposition is equivalent to a convex representation \(x/\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)=\sum_i\lambda_i a_i\) with \(\lambda_i\ge0\) and \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\), after allowing the origin when necessary.
special_cases_latex: For coordinate atoms \(\{\pm e_i\}\), the canonical decomposition has cost \(\sum_i|x_i|\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If the infimum is not attained, then for every \(\varepsilon>0\) an \(\varepsilon\)-atomic decomposition exists whenever the unclosed finite-decomposition value equals the gauge value.
boundary_notes: Closure of the atomic hull can produce points whose gauge value is approached only by a sequence of decompositions.
Decompositions need not be unique.

notation.meaning: Allowed additive excess above the optimal atomic weight.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Atomic Polar Evaluation and Maximizing-Atom Oracle
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be finite-dimensional, let \(\mathcal A\subseteq X\) be nonempty, let \(C=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A\cup\{0\})\), and let \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}=\gamma_C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact support optimization for finite-dimensional atomic gauges; the maximizing atom may fail to exist for noncompact atom sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The atomic polar-oracle interface is the support-optimization identity \[\gamma_{\mathcal A}^\circ(y)=\sigma_C(y)=\sup_{a\in\mathcal A\cup\{0\}}\langle y,a\rangle,\qquad y\in X^*.\] An exact maximizing-atom oracle is a map \(\mathcal O:X^*\rightrightarrows\mathcal A\cup\{0\}\) with \[\mathcal O(y)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{a\in\mathcal A\cup\{0\}}\langle y,a\rangle.\] An \(\varepsilon\)-oracle returns \(a_\varepsilon\) satisfying \(\langle y,a_\varepsilon\rangle\ge\gamma_{\mathcal A}^\circ(y)-\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polar of an atomic gauge is evaluated by maximizing the dual pairing over the atoms. An exact oracle returns a maximizing atom, while an approximate oracle returns an atom whose pairing is within \(\varepsilon\) of the polar value. Convexifying the atom set does not alter this support value.
assumptions_latex: For an exact nonempty oracle value, the support supremum must be attained.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}^\circ(y)\le1\iff \langle y,a\rangle\le1\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\).
special_cases_latex: For a symmetric atom set, \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}^\circ(y)=\sup_{a\in\mathcal A}|\langle y,a\rangle|\) when \(\mathcal A\) is listed without duplicated signs.
For a finite dictionary, the supremum is a finite maximum.
immediate_consequences_latex: A polar unit-ball membership test is equivalent to checking all atomic linear inequalities.
boundary_notes: An oracle for the polar value does not by itself provide an atomic decomposition of a primal point.
For noncompact atom sets, exact argmax sets may be empty even when the supremum is finite.

notation.meaning: Set of atoms maximizing the pairing with \(y\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(z\in X\), define the polar gauge by
\[
\gamma_C^{\circ}(z)=\sup\{\langle z,x\rangle:\gamma_C(x)\le1\}.
\]
Because the unit sublevel set of \(\gamma_C\) is \(C\),
\[
\gamma_C^{\circ}(z)=\sigma_C(z)=\sup_{x\in C}\langle z,x\rangle
=\sup_{a\in\mathcal A}\langle z,a\rangle.
\]
If \(\mathcal A=-\mathcal A\), the same value is \(\sup_{a\in\mathcal A}|\langle z,a\rangle|\). All suprema are understood in the extended real line.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate an atomic polar gauge by maximizing the linear pairing over the atoms; use the absolute pairing when the atomic set is symmetric.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(z\in X\) and tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), compute
\[
s_{\mathcal A}(z)=\sup_{a\in\mathcal A}\langle z,a\rangle
\]
and return an atom \(a_\varepsilon\in\mathcal A\) satisfying
\[
\langle z,a_\varepsilon\rangle\ge s_{\mathcal A}(z)-\varepsilon.
\]
If no such atom exists, the oracle reports nonattainment at the requested tolerance. For \(\varepsilon=0\), a successful output is an exact support point. The oracle output consists of the value \(\langle z,a_\varepsilon\rangle\), the atom \(a_\varepsilon\), and the declared tolerance \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A support oracle returns an atom whose pairing with the query direction is within a declared additive tolerance of the atomic support value.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(z\in X\),
\[
\gamma_C^{\circ}(z)=\sigma_C(z)=\sigma_{\mathcal A}(z)=\sup_{a\in\mathcal A}\langle z,a\rangle.
\]
Consequently, polar-gauge evaluation and atomic linear optimization have the same value. An atom \(a\in\mathcal A\) is an exact oracle output precisely when \(\langle z,a\rangle=\gamma_C^{\circ}(z)\). For \(\varepsilon\ge 0\), it is additive-\(\varepsilon\) optimal precisely when \(\langle z,a\rangle\ge\gamma_C^{\circ}(z)-\varepsilon\). This equivalence concerns values and atomic-output tests; it does not assert that every optimizer over \(C\) is an atom.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Atomic polar evaluation and atomic linear optimization have the same value, and an atom satisfies the exact or approximate oracle criterion exactly when its pairing satisfies the corresponding polar-value test.

children.title: Oracle Attainment Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits caused by nonattainment or noncompact atomic sets.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.
\(\mathcal A\subset X\) is nonempty, and support values are taken in the extended real line.
An exact atomic oracle must return an atom attaining the support value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\mathcal A\) is compact, every support value is finite and attained; without compactness, finite nonattainment or infinite support can occur.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional distinction among compact attainment, finite nonattainment, and infinite support.

source_refs.locator: 7.1 Support Points p. 133
source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Monotone Operator Theory in Hilbert Spaces

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(\mathcal A\) is compact, then for every \(z\in X\), the value \(\sigma_{\mathcal A}(z)=\sup_{a\in\mathcal A}\langle z,a\rangle\) is finite and is attained by some \(a^\star\in\mathcal A\). Compactness cannot simply be discarded: for \(X=\mathbb R\), \(\mathcal A=(0,1)\), and \(z=1\),
\[
\sigma_{\mathcal A}(1)=1,
\]
but no atom attains this value. Unboundedness creates a second boundary: for \(\mathcal A=[0,\infty)\) and \(z=1\), the support value is \(+\infty\). Hence an exact atomic oracle may fail through either finite nonattainment or an infinite objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In finite dimensions, compact atomic sets have finite attained support values. Noncompact sets can have a finite unattained supremum, and unbounded sets can have infinite support.
knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Attainment Boundaries

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closedness Does Not Ensure Support Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A closed convex unbounded atomic set with a finite unattained support value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[\mathcal A=\{(u,v)\in\mathbb R^2:v\ge e^u\},\qquad z=(0,-1).\] Then \(\mathcal A\) is closed and convex and \[\sigma_{\mathcal A}(z)=\sup_{(u,v)\in\mathcal A}(-v)=0,\] but every \((u,v)\in\mathcal A\) satisfies \(-v<0\). Thus the finite support value is not attained despite closedness and convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex atomic set can have a finite but unattained support value; closedness alone cannot replace compactness.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional real vector spaces, let \(A:X\to Y\) be linear, let \(b\in Y\), and let \(\mathcal A\subseteq X\) be a symmetric atom set encoding elementary sparse components. Let \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal A}\) be its atomic norm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex sparse recovery; coordinate and grouped atoms are included, while continuous-measure atoms are treated separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sparse recovery gauge model is \[\inf_{x\in X}\{\|x\|_{\mathcal A}:\rho(b-Ax)\le\sigma\},\] where \(\rho\) is a residual gauge and \(\sigma\ge0\). Equivalently, using atomic coefficients, it minimizes total absolute atomic weight among decompositions \(x=\sum_i\alpha_i a_i\) whose synthesized signal satisfies the fidelity constraint. The penalized form is \[\inf_x\{L(Ax,b)+\lambda\|x\|_{\mathcal A}\},\qquad\lambda\ge0,\] for a proper convex data-fit function \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse recovery is modeled by choosing atoms that represent individual allowable components and minimizing the atomic norm subject to data fidelity, or adding it as a convex penalty. Coordinate atoms give ordinary \(\ell_1\) recovery, while block-supported atoms give group-sparse gauges.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A=-\mathcal A\) and its convex hull is absorbing on the modeled subspace.
\(\rho\) is a residual gauge with \(\sigma\ge0\), or \(L\) is a proper convex loss with \(\lambda\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The structural objective equals the minimum total absolute coefficient weight over atomic representations compatible with the fidelity model.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For exact data, \(\rho=\delta_{\{0\}}\) gives \(\inf\{\|x\|_{\mathcal A}:Ax=b\}\).
special_cases_latex: With \(\mathcal A=\{\pm e_i\}\), the exact model is basis pursuit \(\inf\{\|x\|_1:Ax=b\}\).
With atoms supported on prescribed groups and Euclidean-normalized within each group, the gauge is a group-sparsity norm.
immediate_consequences_latex: The polar structural cost is the largest correlation of a dual vector with any sparse atom.
boundary_notes: The definition specifies a convex surrogate and does not assert recovery of the sparsest feasible representation.
Nonconvex \(\ell_0\) minimization is outside this gauge family.

notation.meaning: Symmetric atomic gauge generated by \(\mathcal A\).

children.title: Coordinate Sparsity Gauges
children.top_down_role: Gauge models for coordinate-sparse vectors.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional coordinate sparsity with strictly positive weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(w_i>0\), let
\[
\mathcal A_w=\{\pm w_i^{-1}e_i:1\leq i\leq n\}.
\]
Then
\[
\gamma_{\mathcal A_w}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^nw_i|x_i|,
\qquad
\gamma_{\mathcal A_w}^{\circ}(z)=\max_i\frac{|z_i|}{w_i}.
\]
Zero weights make the normalized atoms undefined, and signed weights do not define this positive weighted-norm convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rescaling signed coordinate atoms gives the weighted one-norm and its reciprocal-weight infinity polar.
review_flags: Strict positivity is required for the stated normalization and norm interpretation.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Coordinate Atomic Gauges

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate vectors restricted to the infinity-norm unit cube.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\|x\|_0=|\{i:x_i\neq0\}|\). On
\[
B_\infty=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\|x\|_\infty\leq1\},
\]
the greatest convex function bounded above by \(\|x\|_0\) is
\[
\operatorname{conv}_{B_\infty}(\|\cdot\|_0)(x)=\|x\|_1.
\]
Thus the signed-coordinate atomic gauge is the convex envelope of cardinality under \(|x_i|\leq1\). Without an amplitude-bounded domain, \(\|\cdot\|_1\) is not the global convex envelope of scale-invariant cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the infinity-norm unit cube, the one-norm is exactly the convex envelope of coordinate cardinality.
assumptions_latex: The convex envelope is taken relative to \(B_\infty\).
review_flags: The amplitude-bounded domain is essential and must accompany the convex-envelope claim.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Envelope of Coordinate Cardinality

review_flags: A supplied locator specifically supporting the coordinate atomic-gauge identification is absent.
standard_field_rationale: signed coordinate atoms generate the cross-polytope, whose gauge and support are the one- and infinity-norms.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical convex gauge for coordinate-sparse vectors in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The closed convex hull of the signed coordinate atoms is
\[
\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\|x\|_1\le1\}.
\]
Consequently its atomic gauge and polar gauge are
\[
\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n|x_i|=\|x\|_1,
\qquad
\gamma_{\mathcal A}^{\circ}(z)=\max_{1\le i\le n}|z_i|=\|z\|_\infty.
\]
Equivalently, \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)\) is the minimum coefficient mass of a signed-coordinate decomposition of \(x\), while the polar selects the coordinate having largest absolute pairing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Signed coordinate atoms yield the one-norm gauge, whose polar is the infinity norm and whose decompositions expose coordinate sparsity.
knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Sparsity Gauges

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The signed-coordinate atomic gauge and polar formulas are correct and fit the representation container, but no inspectable source locator is supplied.

children.title: Structured Sparsity Gauge Family
children.top_down_role: Gauge models for grouped and combinatorial support structures.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(I=\{1,\ldots,N\}\), let \(\mathcal G\) be a finite collection of nonempty subsets of \(I\) whose union is \(I\), and let \(p\in[1,+\infty)\). For each \(G\in\mathcal G\), let \(X_G=\{z\in\mathbb R^N:\operatorname{supp}z\subseteq G\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional grouped and overlapping-group sparsity; this is the latent decomposition gauge, which differs from directly summing norms of overlapping subvectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The latent group structured-sparsity gauge is \[\Omega_{\mathcal G,p}(x)=\inf\left\{\sum_{G\in\mathcal G}w_G\|z_G\|_p:z_G\in X_G,\ \sum_{G\in\mathcal G}z_G=x\right\},\] where \(w_G>0\) are prescribed group weights. Its unit set is the convex hull of the weighted group atoms \[\mathcal A=\bigcup_{G\in\mathcal G}\{z\in X_G:w_G\|z\|_p\le1\}.\] Thus \(\Omega_{\mathcal G,p}\) is an atomic gauge whose decompositions allocate the signal among allowed support groups.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gauge decomposes a vector into components supported on prescribed groups and charges the weighted sum of their within-group norms. Overlapping groups are handled by optimizing the allocation of shared coordinates. The same functional is the atomic gauge of the union of the weighted group unit balls.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal G\) is finite, each group is nonempty, and \(\bigcup_{G\in\mathcal G}G=I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Omega_{\mathcal G,p}=\gamma_{\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)}\), with \(\mathcal A\) equal to the union of weighted group unit balls.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(L((z_G)_G)=\sum_Gz_G\) and \(f((z_G)_G)=\sum_Gw_G\|z_G\|_p\), one has \(\Omega_{\mathcal G,p}=L\mathbin{\triangleright}f\), the infimal postcomposition.
special_cases_latex: If the groups form a partition and \(w_G=1\), then \(\Omega_{\mathcal G,p}(x)=\sum_G\|x_G\|_p\).
Singleton groups with \(p=1\) recover the \(\ell_1\) norm.
immediate_consequences_latex: The gauge promotes representations using few active groups because inactive components have \(z_G=0\).
boundary_notes: For overlapping groups, this latent gauge generally differs from \(\sum_Gw_G\|x_G\|_p\), which counts shared coordinates repeatedly.
The group family and weights are model inputs, not inferred by the definition.

notation.meaning: Infimal postcomposition of \(f\) by the synthesis map \(L\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact proximal map for the nonoverlapping weighted group gauge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\lambda\ge0\),
\[
\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda\Omega}(x)\bigr)_g=
\begin{cases}
\left(1-\dfrac{\lambda w_g}{\|x_g\|_2}\right)_+x_g,&x_g\ne0,\\
0,&x_g=0.
\end{cases}
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal map independently shrinks each block radially and deletes blocks below their weighted thresholds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The proximal map is block soft-thresholding.

notation.meaning: Proximal map of the scaled gauge.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subdifferential of the Weighted Group Gauge
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonoverlapping positive-weight Euclidean groups.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\Omega(x)=\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}w_g\|x_g\|_2\), one has \(z\in\partial\Omega(x)\) exactly when
\[
z_g=w_g\frac{x_g}{\|x_g\|_2}\quad(x_g\ne0),
\qquad \|z_g\|_2\le w_g\quad(x_g=0)
\]
for every group \(g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The subgradient is the weighted unit direction on active blocks and belongs to the corresponding weighted Euclidean ball on inactive blocks.
knowledge_statements.title: Subdifferential of the Weighted Group Gauge

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal G\) is a partition of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) into nonempty groups.

notation.meaning: Restriction of a vector to group coordinates.

review_flags: No group-sparsity source locator was supplied.
standard_field_rationale: standard weighted block one-over-two norm and its dual norm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonoverlapping weighted group gauge and its polar norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), define the weighted group-sparsity gauge by
\[
\Omega(x)=\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}w_g\|x_g\|_2.
\]
Because the groups form a partition and all weights are positive, \(\Omega\) is a norm. Its polar norm is
\[
\Omega^{\circ}(z)=\max_{g\in\mathcal G}\frac{\|z_g\|_2}{w_g}.
\]
The gauge aggregates group magnitudes with an outer one-norm, whereas its polar tests the largest weight-normalized group magnitude. Singleton groups with unit weights recover the coordinate one-norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The weighted sum of Euclidean block norms is a group-sparsity norm; its polar is the largest weight-normalized block norm.
knowledge_statements.title: Group Sparsity Gauges

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nonoverlapping weighted block norm and its polar are correct, and definition is an appropriate primary kind for this gauge container. A supporting source locator is absent.

children.title: Overlapping-Group Gauges
children.top_down_role: Gauge models for collections of groups with shared variables.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact certificate for a proposed decomposition attaining the latent overlapping-group gauge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x=\sum_gv^g\) with \(\operatorname{supp}(v^g)\subseteq g\). This decomposition attains \(\Omega_{\mathrm{lat}}(x)=\sum_gw_g\|v^g\|_2\) if and only if there exists \(z\) such that
\[
\|z_g\|_2\le w_g\quad\forall g,
\qquad z_g=w_g\frac{v^g}{\|v^g\|_2}\quad\text{whenever }v^g\ne0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A latent allocation is optimal exactly when one polar-feasible vector simultaneously supports every nonzero group component.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal G\) is finite, covers all coordinates, and \(w_g>0\).
The proposed group-supported components sum to \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The decomposition is gauge-minimizing exactly when the common supporting vector exists.

notation.meaning: Restriction of the common certificate to group \(g\).

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal Latent-Decomposition Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct repeated-charging convention, distinct from the latent gauge in the seed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite covering family \(\mathcal G\), define
\[
\Omega_{\mathrm{dir}}(x)=\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}w_g\|x_g\|_2.
\]
Its polar norm is
\[
\Omega_{\mathrm{dir}}^\circ(z)=\inf\left\{t\ge0:z=\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}z^g,\ \operatorname{supp}(z^g)\subseteq g,\ \|z^g\|_2\le tw_g\ \forall g\right\}.
\]
Unlike the latent gauge, a coordinate contributes directly to every containing group.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Theta\) be a compact Hausdorff parameter space, let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space, and let \(a:\Theta\to X\) be continuous. Let \(\mathcal M(\Theta)\) be the finite signed Radon measures on \(\Theta\), with total-variation norm \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\), and define \(\Phi\mu=\int_\Theta a(\theta)\,d\mu(\theta)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous-dictionary sparse recovery through finite signed measures on a compact parameter space; discretized grids are not part of the definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The off-grid sparse-measure gauge on \(\operatorname{range}\Phi\) is \[\gamma_{a}(x)=\inf\{\|\mu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}:\mu\in\mathcal M(\Theta),\ \Phi\mu=x\}.\] It is the atomic gauge generated by \(\mathcal A=\{\pm a(\theta):\theta\in\Theta\}\). An off-grid recovery model therefore has the form \[\inf_{\mu\in\mathcal M(\Theta)}\{\|\mu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}:\rho(b-A\Phi\mu)\le\sigma\}.\] For an atomic measure \(\mu=\sum_{i=1}^mc_i\delta_{\theta_i}\), its cost is \(\|\mu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=\sum_i|c_i|\) after combining repeated locations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous parameter space supplies atoms without choosing a finite grid. A signed measure records atom locations and amplitudes, the synthesis map integrates the atom map against that measure, and total variation measures coefficient mass. Minimizing total variation subject to data fidelity is therefore the continuous-dictionary counterpart of finite-dimensional \(\ell_1\) recovery.
assumptions_latex: \(\Theta\) is compact Hausdorff and \(a:\Theta\to X\) is continuous.
\(\mathcal M(\Theta)\) consists of finite signed Radon measures.
\(A:X\to Y\) is linear, \(\rho\) is a residual gauge, and \(\sigma\ge0\) for the recovery model.

special_cases_latex: If \(\Theta\) is finite, measures reduce to coefficient vectors and total variation reduces to the \(\ell_1\) norm.
A finitely supported measure represents a sparse off-grid superposition \(\sum_i c_i a(\theta_i)\).

boundary_notes: Existence or uniqueness of a sparsest representing measure is not asserted.
For complex measures the symmetric atom set must include all unit-modulus phases; that variant is outside this real formulation.

For \(\mu\in\mathcal M(\Theta)\), define the sparse-measure gauge by
\[
\|\mu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=|\mu|(\Theta),
\]
where \(|\mu|\) is the variation measure. Its unit ball is the closed convex hull, in the natural weak-star topology, of the signed Dirac atoms \(\{\pm\delta_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}\). In particular, if

\mu=\sum_{j=1}^{k}c_j\delta_{\theta_j}
\]

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth convex minimization over a bounded continuous atomic ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[
\min_{y\in\tau\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)}f(y),\qquad
\mathcal A=\{\pm\phi(\theta):\theta\in\Theta\}.
\]
At \(y_k\), choose
\[
\theta_k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\theta\in\Theta}|\langle\nabla f(y_k),\phi(\theta)\rangle|
\]
and a sign minimizing the gradient pairing, obtaining \(s_k\in\tau\mathcal A\). Then
\[
y_{k+1}=(1-\eta_k)y_k+\eta_ks_k
\]
remains feasible and adds at most one continuously located signed atom.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Off-grid Frank-Wolfe uses a global continuous maximum-correlation search and adds at most one atom per iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable and convex on \(\tau\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A maximum-absolute-correlation signed atom solves the Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem.

notation.meaning: Selected signed atom scaled by tau

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori Frank-Wolfe certificate using the global continuous-dictionary polar oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For feasible \(y\in\tau\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\), define
\[
g(y)=\langle\nabla f(y),y\rangle+\tau\gamma_{\mathcal A}^{\circ}(-\nabla f(y)).
\]
Then
\[
0\leq f(y)-f^*\leq g(y).
\]
Thus \(g(y)\leq\varepsilon\) certifies \(\varepsilon\)-optimality. The certificate is rigorous only when the continuous supremum is evaluated globally or bounded above rigorously; a grid maximum alone can underestimate the gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The continuous polar correlation gives a Frank-Wolfe gap certifying objective suboptimality, whereas an uncorrected grid maximum does not.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditional-Gradient Rate with an Exact Off-Grid Oracle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact continuous linear minimization and finite Frank-Wolfe curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C_f<\infty\) be the Frank-Wolfe curvature of \(f\) on \(\tau\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\). If every continuous linear-minimization subproblem is solved exactly and \(\eta_k=2/(k+2)\), then
\[
f(y_k)-f^*\leq\frac{2C_f}{k+2}.
\]
After \(k\) updates, \(y_k\) is a convex combination of at most \(k+1\) selected signed atoms. Approximate atom searches require an explicit oracle-error term; the displayed bound cannot otherwise be asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact off-grid Frank-Wolfe has the standard O(1/k) objective bound and a linear support-size bound.
assumptions_latex: The continuous linear-minimization oracle is exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(y_k)-f^*\leq2C_f/(k+2)\), with at most \(k+1\) selected atoms after \(k\) updates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dense-Grid Recovery of the Continuous Gauge
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested finite grids for a compact continuous dictionary with an absorbing atomic hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Theta\) be compact, let \(a:\Theta\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuous, and let finite grids \(G_k\subseteq G_{k+1}\subseteq\Theta\) have dense union. Define
\[
\mathcal A_k=\{\pm a(\theta):\theta\in G_k\},\qquad
\mathcal A=\{\pm a(\theta):\theta\in\Theta\}.
\]
If \(0\in\operatorname{int}\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\), then
\[
\gamma_{\mathcal A_k}(x)\downarrow\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)
\]
for every \(x\), uniformly on compact subsets of \(\mathbb R^n\). The interior assumption ensures eventual absorption by the grid hulls and finiteness in every direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested dense grids recover an absorbing compact continuous atomic gauge monotonically from above.
assumptions_latex: Each \(G_k\) is finite, the grids are nested, and their union is dense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_{\mathcal A_k}\downarrow\gamma_{\mathcal A}\) pointwise and uniformly on compact sets.
review_flags: No universal convergence rate follows without quantitative regularity and grid-coverage assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Dense-Grid Recovery of the Continuous Gauge

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of an absorbing continuous atomic ball with an inner grid approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B_G\subseteq B\) be closed convex origin-containing sets and suppose
\[
\rho B\subseteq B_G
\]
for some \(0<\rho\leq1\). Then
\[
\gamma_B(x)\leq\gamma_{B_G}(x)\leq\rho^{-1}\gamma_B(x)
\]
for every \(x\), while
\[
\rho\gamma_B^{\circ}(z)\leq\gamma_{B_G}^{\circ}(z)\leq\gamma_B^{\circ}(z)
\]
for every \(z\). Without a positive inclusion factor, grid density alone gives no uniform relative gauge bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A grid has a uniform multiplicative gauge guarantee when its hull contains a fixed positive scaling of the continuous atomic ball.
review_flags: The containment condition is sufficient and, with the best possible rho, exactly encodes the uniform multiplicative comparison.

\[

with the left side possibly \(+\infty\), and
\[

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multiplicative Approximation Criterion for a Discretized Atomic Ball
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative comparison of an absorbing continuous atomic ball and an inner grid approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
B=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A),\qquad B_G=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A_G),
\]
with \(B_G\subseteq B\), and suppose that for some \(0<\rho\leq1\),
\[
\rho B\subseteq B_G.
\]
Then for every \(x\),
\[
\gamma_B(x)\leq\gamma_{B_G}(x)\leq\rho^{-1}\gamma_B(x),
\]
and for every \(z\),
\[
\rho\,\gamma_B^{\circ}(z)
\leq\gamma_{B_G}^{\circ}(z)
\leq\gamma_B^{\circ}(z).
\]
Without a positive inclusion factor \(\rho\), grid density alone supplies no uniform relative-error bound for the gauge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A grid gives a uniform multiplicative gauge approximation exactly when its atomic hull contains a fixed positive scaling of the continuous atomic ball.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathbb{F}\in\{\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C}\}\), let \(X\in\mathbb{F}^{m\times n}\), let \(q=\min\{m,n\}\), and write \(\sigma(X)=(\sigma_1(X),\ldots,\sigma_q(X))\) for the singular values in nonincreasing order.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional matrix models whose structural regularizer is a convex unitarily invariant gauge of the singular-value vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi:\mathbb{R}_+^q\to[0,+\infty]\) be convex, positively homogeneous, lower semicontinuous, and invariant under coordinate permutations; when extended to \(\mathbb{R}^q\), assume invariance under sign changes. The associated spectral gauge is \(\kappa_\phi(X)=\phi(\sigma(X))\). A low-rank spectral gauge model is an optimization model in which \(\kappa_\phi(X)\) is used as an objective, constraint, or level-set parameter to encode singular-value structure. Its unit ball is \(C_\phi=\{X:\phi(\sigma(X))\le1\}\), and its polar gauge is \(\kappa_\phi^\circ(Y)=\phi^\circ(\sigma(Y))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A low-rank spectral gauge is obtained by applying a convex, positively homogeneous, permutation-invariant scalar gauge to the singular values of a matrix. The resulting matrix function is invariant under left and right unitary transformations. A low-rank spectral gauge model uses that function as a regularizer, constraint, or level-set parameter. Its unit ball consists exactly of matrices whose singular-value vectors lie in the scalar gauge ball, and its polar is obtained by applying the polar scalar gauge to the singular values.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\kappa_\phi(UXV^*)=\kappa_\phi(X)\) for all compatible unitary matrices \(U,V\).
special_cases_latex: For \(\phi(s)=\|s\|_1\), \(\kappa_\phi(X)=\|X\|_*\), the nuclear norm.
For \(\phi(s)=\|s\|_\infty\), \(\kappa_\phi(X)=\|X\|_{\mathrm{op}}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The nuclear-norm unit ball is the closed convex hull of unit-norm rank-one matrix atoms.
boundary_notes: Not every spectral gauge promotes low rank; the nuclear norm is the canonical convex rank-one atomic gauge.
The definition does not include nonconvex rank penalties or Schatten quasi-norms with exponent below one.

notation.meaning: Ordered singular-value vector of the matrix.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Balanced Atomic Gauge Generated by Rank-One Matrices
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(E=\mathbb{F}^m\) and \(F=\mathbb{F}^n\) be finite-dimensional inner-product spaces. Let \(U\subset E\) and \(V\subset F\) be compact, balanced sets that span their respective spaces and contain no requirement of convexity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional balanced matrix gauges generated by outer products; asymmetric or positive-semidefinite-only atomic families are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the rank-one atomic set \(\mathcal A=\{uv^*:u\in U,\ v\in V\}\) and its closed convex hull \(C=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\). The associated rank-one matrix gauge is \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}(X)=\inf\{t\ge0:X\in tC\}\). Equivalently, \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}(X)=\inf\{\sum_{j=1}^r c_j:X=\sum_{j=1}^r c_j u_jv_j^*,\ c_j\ge0,\ u_j\in U,\ v_j\in V,\ r\in\mathbb N\}\). Its polar gauge is \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}^\circ(Y)=\sup_{u\in U,v\in V}|\langle Y,uv^*\rangle|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose balanced spanning sets of left and right factors and form every admissible rank-one outer product. The rank-one matrix gauge is the Minkowski functional of the closed convex hull of those atoms. It is also the smallest total nonnegative coefficient weight among all finite atomic decompositions of the matrix. The polar gauge is the largest absolute pairing of a dual matrix with an admissible rank-one atom.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(U\) and \(V\) are unit balls of gauges \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\), then \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}(X)=\inf\{\sum_j\alpha(u_j)\beta(v_j):X=\sum_j u_jv_j^*\}\).
special_cases_latex: With Euclidean unit spheres for \(U\) and \(V\), \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}(X)=\|X\|_*\) and \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}^\circ(Y)=\|Y\|_{\mathrm{op}}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every atom \(a\in\mathcal A\) satisfies \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}(a)\le1\).
boundary_notes: If the atomic family does not span the matrix space, the gauge may take value \(+\infty\).
Removing balance generally produces an asymmetric gauge and removes the absolute value from the support formula.

Let \(\mathcal A_1=\{uv^{\mathsf T}:\|u\|_2=\|v\|_2=1\}\). The gauge of \(\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A_1)\) satisfies

\]
Thus the nuclear unit ball and operator-norm unit ball are polar to one another.

children.title: Trace-Norm Gauge Conventions
children.top_down_role: Trace-norm terminology and domain-specific representation choices.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional real symmetric or complex Hermitian matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(H=H^*\) has eigenvalues \(\lambda_1(H),\ldots,\lambda_n(H)\), then
\[
\|H\|_* = \sum_{i=1}^n|\lambda_i(H)|=\operatorname{tr}|H|.
\]
Consequently, \(\|H\|_*=\operatorname{tr}(H)\) if and only if \(H\succeq0\), while \(\|H\|_*=-\operatorname{tr}(H)\) if and only if \(H\preceq0\). In general \(|\operatorname{tr}(H)|\leq\|H\|_*\), with strict inequality possible through cancellation of positive and negative eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For Hermitian matrices the trace norm is the sum of absolute eigenvalues and equals the ordinary trace exactly in the PSD regime.
assumptions_latex: \(H=H^*\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}\), or \(H\in\mathbb S^n\) in the real case.
review_flags: Standard spectral-theorem specialization; ordinary trace must not be substituted outside the PSD regime.
knowledge_statements.title: Hermitian Trace-Norm Convention

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a real or complex matrix; in the complex case the adjoint replaces the transpose.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The names nuclear norm, trace norm, and Schatten one-norm denote the same singular-value gauge; trace equality requires positive semidefiniteness.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Terminological convention separating trace norm from the trace functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The terms nuclear norm, trace norm, and Schatten \(1\)-norm are used here synonymously for
\[
\|X\|_*:=\operatorname{tr}\bigl((X^*X)^{1/2}\bigr)=\sum_i\sigma_i(X).
\]
For a Hermitian positive-semidefinite matrix \(X\succeq0\), this gauge reduces to \(\|X\|_*=\operatorname{tr}(X)\). For a general square matrix, \(\operatorname{tr}(X)\) is not a norm and must not be substituted for \(\|X\|_*\); cancellation among eigenvalues can make their values different.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nuclear norm, trace norm, and Schatten one-norm coincide; only on positive-semidefinite matrices does this norm equal the ordinary trace.
knowledge_statements.title: Trace-Norm Gauge Conventions

children.title: Rank-One Atomic Representations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional real matrices; factor width is at least the matrix rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(q\geq\operatorname{rank}(X)\),
\[
\|X\|_* = \min_{LR^{\mathsf T}=X}\frac12\bigl(\|L\|_F^2+\|R\|_F^2\bigr),
\]
where \(L\in\mathbb R^{m\times q}\) and \(R\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}\). Equivalently,
\[
\|X\|_* = \min_{X=\sum_{j=1}^q a_jb_j^{\mathsf T}}\frac12\sum_{j=1}^q\bigl(\|a_j\|_2^2+\|b_j\|_2^2\bigr).
\]
The minima are attained; an SVD gives \(L=U\Sigma^{1/2}\), \(R=V\Sigma^{1/2}\), with zero columns appended if needed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nuclear atomic gauge equals the minimum balanced squared Frobenius mass of a rank-one factorization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Real rectangular matrices with separate row- and column-space PSD blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\),
\[
\|X\|_* = \frac12\min_{W\in\mathbb S^m,\,Z\in\mathbb S^n}
\left\{\operatorname{tr}(W)+\operatorname{tr}(Z):
\begin{bmatrix}W&X\\X^{\mathsf T}&Z\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\right\}.
\]
The minimum is attained. If \(X=U\Sigma V^{\mathsf T}\) is a compact SVD, then \(W=U\Sigma U^{\mathsf T}\) and \(Z=V\Sigma V^{\mathsf T}\) are optimal.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided gauge on the positive-semidefinite cone; inclusion of zero in the generating convex set is essential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B_+=\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup\mathcal A_+)\). Its Minkowski functional is the extended-valued gauge
\[
\gamma_+(X)=
\begin{cases}
\operatorname{tr}(X),&X\succeq0,\\
+\infty,&X\not\succeq0.
\end{cases}
\]
Because \(B_+\) is not centrally symmetric, \(\gamma_+\) is a gauge but not a norm. Under the trace pairing, its polar gauge is
\[
\gamma_+^{\circ}(Y)=\sup_{X\in B_+}\operatorname{tr}(YX)=\max\left\{0,\sup_{\|u\|_2=1}u^{\mathsf T}Yu\right\}=\max\{0,\lambda_{\max}(Y)\}.
\]

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trace minimization over the PSD cone with affine equality measurements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[
\min_{X\succeq0}\operatorname{tr}(X)\quad\text{subject to}\quad A(X)=b,
\]
and let \(X_0\succeq0\) be feasible. If some \(y\) satisfies
\[
A^*y\preceq I,\qquad \langle y,b\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(X_0),
\]
then \(X_0\) is optimal. Equivalently, for \(S=I-A^*y\),
\[
S\succeq0,\qquad SX_0=0.
\]
Thus the dual slack vanishes on the range of \(X_0\) and is nonnegative on its orthogonal complement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PSD trace-minimization candidate is certified by a PSD dual slack annihilating its range.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(A^*y\preceq I\) and \(\langle y,b\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(X_0)\), then \(X_0\) is optimal.
review_flags: This is the eigenspace analogue of the rectangular singular-space certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Semidefinite Spectral Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained nuclear-norm minimization at a fixed feasible matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a feasible matrix \(X_0\), define
\[
\mathcal D_*(X_0)=\{H:\exists t>0\text{ with }\|X_0+tH\|_*\leq\|X_0\|_*\}.
\]
Then \(X_0\) is the unique solution of
\[
\min_X\|X\|_*\quad\text{subject to}\quad A(X)=A(X_0)
\]
if and only if
\[
\ker A\cap\mathcal D_*(X_0)=\{0\}.
\]
A strict tangent-space spectral certificate together with injectivity of \(A\) on the tangent space is a standard sufficient condition for this exact test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nuclear-norm recovery is unique exactly when the measurement nullspace contains no nonzero descent direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X_0\) is uniquely optimal if and only if \(\ker A\cap\mathcal D_*(X_0)=\{0\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T=\{UB^{\mathsf T}+CV^{\mathsf T}:B\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r},\ C\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times r}\}\). A matrix \(Y=A^*y\) is a spectral dual certificate for minimizing \(\|X\|_*\) subject to \(A(X)=A(X_0)\) when
\[
P_T(Y)=UV^{\mathsf T},\qquad \|P_{T^\perp}(Y)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq1.
\]
These conditions are equivalent to \(Y\in\partial\|X_0\|_*\) and certify optimality. If the second inequality is strict and \(A\) is injective on \(T\), the certificate supplies the standard strict exposure conditions used to establish uniqueness.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional vector space, let \(\kappa:X\to[0,+\infty]\) be a closed gauge, and let \(\rho:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be a proper closed convex fidelity function.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex gauge models; correspondence means equality or inclusion of solution sets at matched parameters, not universal identity of formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\tau,\sigma,\lambda\ge0\), define \(P_\tau=\operatorname*{argmin}\{\rho(x):\kappa(x)\le\tau\}\), \(Q_\sigma=\operatorname*{argmin}\{\kappa(x):\rho(x)\le\sigma\}\), and \(R_\lambda=\operatorname*{argmin}_x\{\rho(x)+\lambda\kappa(x)\}\). Two parameterized formulations correspond at their stated parameters when their solution sets have a common point; they correspond exactly when the solution sets are equal. A point \(x^\star\) gives an active parameter match between the constrained models when \(\tau=\kappa(x^\star)\), \(\sigma=\rho(x^\star)\), and \(x^\star\in P_\tau\cap Q_\sigma\). A multiplier match with the penalized model additionally requires \(0\in\partial\rho(x^\star)+\lambda\partial\kappa(x^\star)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gauge formulation correspondence relates three families built from the same fidelity and structural gauge: fidelity minimization under a gauge bound, gauge minimization under a fidelity bound, and a weighted sum of fidelity and gauge. Correspondence at chosen parameters means that the formulations share a solution; exact correspondence means their entire solution sets coincide. Active constrained parameters are the attained fidelity and gauge values, while correspondence with a penalized model requires a compatible nonnegative multiplier stationarity condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in P_{\kappa(x^\star)}\cap Q_{\rho(x^\star)}\) defines an active constrained correspondence, and \(x^\star\in R_\lambda\) is matched when \(0\in\partial\rho(x^\star)+\lambda\partial\kappa(x^\star)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The constrained pair corresponds at \((\tau,\sigma)\) precisely when \(P_\tau\cap Q_\sigma\ne\varnothing\).
special_cases_latex: For \(\rho(x)=\|Ax-b\|\), the two constrained families are residual minimization with a gauge budget and minimum-gauge recovery with a residual tolerance.
immediate_consequences_latex: Matched formulations have the same attained pair \((\kappa(x^\star),\rho(x^\star))\) at a shared solution.
boundary_notes: Nonunique solutions may yield intersection without equality of solution sets.
A weighted-sum parameter need not represent every boundary solution without convexity and suitable regularity.
The endpoint \(\lambda=0\) can ignore the gauge entirely.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(C_\tau=\{x\in X:\gamma(x)\leq\tau\}\). The gauge-constrained model is
\[
\min_{x\in X}\ f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad x\in C_\tau.
\]
A feasible point \(x_\tau\) is optimal if and only if
\[
0\in\partial f(x_\tau)+N_{C_\tau}(x_\tau).
\]
Under the stated constraint qualification, this is equivalent to the existence of \(\lambda\geq0\) such that
\[
0\in\partial f(x_\tau)+\lambda\partial\gamma(x_\tau),\qquad \lambda\bigl(\gamma(x_\tau)-\tau\bigr)=0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A gauge-constrained model minimizes convex fidelity on a gauge ball; under a Slater-type condition, optimality is characterized equivalently by normal-cone or multiplier subgradient conditions.
knowledge_statements.title: Gauge-Constrained Models

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The gauge-penalized model with parameter \(\lambda>0\) is
\[
\min_{x\in X}\bigl\{f(x)+\lambda\gamma(x)\bigr\}.
\]
A point \(x_\lambda\) is a minimizer if and only if
\[
0\in\partial f(x_\lambda)+\lambda\partial\gamma(x_\lambda),
\]
provided the standard convex subdifferential sum rule applies. Equivalently, there exist \(g\in\partial f(x_\lambda)\) and \(z\in\partial\gamma(x_\lambda)\) satisfying \(g+\lambda z=0\). The parameter \(\lambda\) therefore fixes the supporting tradeoff between fidelity and structural gauge cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gauge penalization minimizes fidelity plus a positive multiple of structural gauge cost; optimality balances their subgradients.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The gauge level-set value function is
\[
v(\tau)=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ \gamma(x)\leq\tau\},\qquad \tau\geq0.
\]
For \(0\leq\tau_1\leq\tau_2\), nested feasible sets give \(v(\tau_2)\leq v(\tau_1)\). Joint convexity of the constraint \(\gamma(x)\leq\tau\) and convexity of \(f\) imply that \(v\) is convex on its effective domain. Thus a target fidelity \(\eta\) can be imposed through the scalar condition \(v(\tau)\leq\eta\), with any attaining \(x_\tau\) solving the corresponding gauge-constrained problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The level-set value function gives optimal fidelity at gauge radius τ; it is nonincreasing and convex and supports scalar parameter searches.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle complexity for locating the least radius meeting a target fidelity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume an exact value oracle for \(v\), a bracket \(0\leq a<b\) with \(v(a)>\eta\geq v(b)\), and a least feasible radius \(\tau_*:=\min\{\tau\in[a,b]:v(\tau)\leq\eta\}\). Bisection using the predicate \(v(\tau)\leq\eta\) maintains \(a_k<\tau_*\leq b_k\) and satisfies \[b_k-a_k=2^{-k}(b-a).\] Thus an interval of length at most \(\varepsilon\) is obtained after \(\lceil\log_2((b-a)/\varepsilon)\rceil\) value-oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact monotone-value bisection locates the least feasible gauge radius to interval accuracy ε in logarithmically many evaluations.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(v(\tau)=\inf\{\rho(x):\kappa(x)\le\tau\}\) and \(w(\sigma)=\inf\{\kappa(x):\rho(x)\le\sigma\}\), with value \(+\infty\) for an empty feasible set. A pair \((\tau,\sigma)\) is a parameter-value correspondence point when \(\sigma=v(\tau)\), \(\tau=w(\sigma)\), and both infima are attained by at least one common point. It is an active correspondence point when every selected common minimizer \(x^\star\) satisfies \(\kappa(x^\star)=\tau\) and \(\rho(x^\star)=\sigma\). The correspondence graph records these mutually minimal attainable boundary pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The first value function gives the least fidelity achievable under a gauge budget, and the second gives the least gauge achievable under a fidelity tolerance. A parameter pair corresponds when each coordinate is the optimal value generated by the other coordinate and the two infima possess a common optimizer. Active correspondence further requires that the optimizer attain both bounds as equalities. This definition separates true boundary correspondence from a merely feasible or slack parameter choice.

boundary_notes: The identities \(\sigma=v(\tau)\) and \(\tau=w(\sigma)\) can fail at flat value-function segments or slack constraints.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_p(\tau):=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\kappa(x)\le\tau}r(x)\) and \(S_v(\sigma):=\operatorname*{argmin}_{r(x)\le\sigma}\kappa(x)\). If \(p(\tau)=\sigma\) and \(v(\sigma)=\tau\), then \[S_p(\tau)=\{x\in X:\kappa(x)=\tau,\ r(x)=\sigma\}=S_v(\sigma).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At mutually corresponding attained parameter values, the two constrained formulations have the same solution set, consisting exactly of points with gauge tau and residual sigma.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solution correspondence between a gauge constraint and positive gauge penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(x_\lambda\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\{f(x)+\lambda\kappa(x)\}\) with \(\lambda>0\), then for \(\tau=\kappa(x_\lambda)\), \[x_\lambda\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\kappa(x)\leq\tau}f(x).\] Conversely, if \(x_\tau\) solves \(\min\{f(x):\kappa(x)\leq\tau\}\) and its KKT system admits \(\lambda>0\), then \[x_\tau\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\{f(x)+\lambda\kappa(x)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A penalized solution solves the constraint at its attained radius, and a constrained solution is recovered by any positive supporting KKT multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper convex and \(\kappa\) is a convex gauge.
For the converse, the constrained solution admits the stated positive KKT multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda>0\text{ and KKT support imply constraint–penalty solution correspondence}.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The equivalence of optimal solution sets is not guaranteed if \(\sigma\ne p(\tau)\), \(\tau\ne v(\sigma)\), or either defining infimum is unattained. A flat portion of the attainable tradeoff frontier can make several budgets share one value, so generalized inverses need not recover the original parameter. Without attainment, \(p(\tau)=\sigma\) need not provide any \(x\) with \(\kappa(x)\le\tau\) and \(r(x)=\sigma\). Thus value equality alone, without mutual correspondence and attainment, does not establish formulation equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Flat tradeoff frontiers, unmatched parameters, infinite values, or unattained infima can destroy parameter recovery and equality of optimal solution sets.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attained convex example not recoverable by a strictly positive gauge penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb R\), \(f(x)=(x-1)^2\), \(\kappa(x)=|x|\), and \(\tau=1\). The problem \[\min\{(x-1)^2:|x|\leq1\}\] has unique solution \(x=1\), and its only KKT multiplier is \(0\). For every \(\lambda>0\), the unique minimizer of \[(x-1)^2+\lambda|x|\] is \(x_\lambda=\max\{1-\lambda/2,0\}<1\). Thus no positive penalty parameter recovers the constrained solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constrained boundary solution having only a zero multiplier can be missed by every positive penalty parameter.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Multiplier Failure of Positive-Penalty Recovery

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed and convex with \(0\in C\), and let \(\kappa_C(x)=\inf\{t\ge0:x\in tC\}\). Let \(C^\circ=\{y:\langle y,x\rangle\le1\ \forall x\in C\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional computational access model; complexity claims are relative to a specified encoding, arithmetic model, accuracy, and bounded query domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A gauge tractability interface for \((C,\kappa_C,C^\circ,\kappa_C^\circ)\) is a declared collection of exact or approximate procedures chosen from: evaluation \(x\mapsto\kappa_C(x)\); membership for \(x\in tC\); separation from \(tC\); support optimization \(y\mapsto\sup_{x\in C}\langle y,x\rangle\); polar membership for \(y\in sC^\circ\); and proximal or projection operations. The interface is polynomially tractable when every declared procedure returns its specified output within time polynomial in the encoded instance size and, for approximate procedures, in \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\) or the stated accuracy measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A gauge tractability interface states exactly how an algorithm may access a gauge ball and its polar. Permitted primitives can include value evaluation, scaled-ball membership, separation, support optimization, polar membership, projection, or proximal evaluation. The interface must say whether each primitive is exact or approximate and must specify the input encoding and accuracy convention. It is polynomially tractable only relative to those choices, when each promised primitive has polynomial running time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak I(C)\subseteq\{\mathrm{Eval}_{\kappa_C},\mathrm{Mem}_{tC},\mathrm{Sep}_{tC},\mathrm{Supp}_C,\mathrm{Mem}_{sC^\circ},\mathrm{Proj}_C,\mathrm{Prox}_{\kappa_C}\}\) together with exactness, accuracy, and complexity specifications defines the interface.
special_cases_latex: An explicit conic representation supplies an implementation of several interface primitives when the associated conic problems are tractable.
An atomic set may instead provide only a support-optimization oracle.
immediate_consequences_latex: Tractability of one primitive must not be silently interpreted as tractability of every other primitive.
boundary_notes: Polynomial equivalences between membership, separation, and optimization require additional geometric and numerical assumptions.
The definition excludes an unspecified black box whose accuracy and cost are not declared.

notation.meaning: Declared collection of computational primitives for the gauge geometry.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Explicit Representation of a Gauge Ball and Epigraph
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a closed convex set containing \(0\), and let \(\kappa_C\) be its Minkowski gauge. Representations may use finitely many auxiliary variables but must have finite encoded data.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional exact representations by explicit inequalities, equations, or finite-dimensional lifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An explicit representation of \(\kappa_C\) is finite data defining either its unit ball \(C=\{x:\exists z,\ F(x,z)\in D\}\) or its epigraph \(\operatorname{epi}\kappa_C=\{(x,t):\exists z,\ G(x,t,z)\in D,\ t\ge0\}\), where the maps, auxiliary dimension, and primitive set \(D\) are specified. The representation is exact when projection eliminates \(z\) to give precisely \(C\) or \(\operatorname{epi}\kappa_C\). For a unit-ball representation, the induced gauge obeys \(\kappa_C(x)=\inf\{t\ge0:\exists z,\ F(x/t,z)\in D\}\), interpreted directly as \(x\in tC\) at \(t=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explicit gauge representation is finite encoded data that describes either the gauge unit ball or the gauge epigraph, possibly as the projection of a finite-dimensional lifted set. Exactness means that eliminating the auxiliary variables yields exactly the intended ball or epigraph, not merely an inner or outer approximation. The gauge value is then the smallest nonnegative scaling for which the point satisfies the represented unit-ball constraints.
equivalent_formulations_latex: An exact unit-ball representation induces the epigraph identity \(\operatorname{epi}\kappa_C=\{(x,t):t\ge0,\ x\in tC\}\), with recession behavior handled at \(t=0\).
special_cases_latex: Taking no auxiliary variable gives a direct representation.
Choosing \(D\) polyhedral, second-order conic, or semidefinite produces the corresponding representation class.
immediate_consequences_latex: Membership in a represented scaled ball reduces to feasibility in the chosen primitive set.
boundary_notes: A finite formula is not automatically computationally tractable; the primitive set and encoding size matter.
Approximate inner or outer descriptions are not exact representations.
review_flags: The supplied representation sources were not inspected for the exact projected-ball and epigraph formulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists z\in\mathbb R^p,\ Ax+Bz\le b\}\) be a nonempty closed convex polyhedron containing \(0\) and absorbing \(\mathbb R^n\). Moreover, \(\gamma_C(x)=0\) exactly when \(x\in\operatorname{rec}C\), equivalently when the displayed system is feasible at \(t=0\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a closed convex polyhedron containing \(0\), and assume a normalized inequality description \(C=\{x:a_i^Tx\le1,\ i=1,\ldots,N\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional polyhedral gauges, allowing asymmetric gauges and zero directions when the unit ball is unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The polyhedral gauge represented by \(C\) is \(\kappa_C(x)=\inf\{t\ge0:a_i^Tx\le t\ \forall i\}\). Whenever this infimum is finite, \(\kappa_C(x)=\max\{0,a_1^Tx,\ldots,a_N^Tx\}\). Its epigraph has the finite linear description \(\operatorname{epi}\kappa_C=\{(x,t):t\ge0,\ a_i^Tx\le t\ \forall i\}\), and its polar unit set is \(C^\circ=\operatorname{conv}\{0,a_1,\ldots,a_N\}\). A lifted polyhedral representation permits additional variables and obtains \(C\) by projection of finitely many linear equalities and inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral gauge is the Minkowski functional of a polyhedral unit set containing the origin. With normalized facet inequalities, its value is the maximum of zero and the finitely many facet linear forms. Consequently, its epigraph is described by finitely many linear inequalities, while its polar unit set is the convex hull of the origin and the facet normals. Auxiliary variables are allowed in a lifted polyhedral representation, provided projection recovers the exact unit set.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A finite vertex-ray description of \(C\) and a finite inequality description are alternative exact polyhedral representations.
special_cases_latex: If \(C\) is centrally symmetric and bounded with nonempty interior, \(\kappa_C\) is a polyhedral norm.
immediate_consequences_latex: Gauge evaluation in the normalized direct representation requires evaluating finitely many linear forms.
boundary_notes: If \(C\) is not absorbing, the gauge can be \(+\infty\) outside its conic hull.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conic and Semidefinite Lift of a Gauge
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^q\) be a closed convex cone, let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) contain \(0\), and let \(\kappa_C\) denote its gauge.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional lifted representations; semidefinite lifts are the specialization in which the primitive cone is a product of positive-semidefinite cones and linear subspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A \(K\)-conic lift of the gauge unit ball is affine data \((A,B,c)\) such that \(C=\{x:\exists z,\ Ax+Bz+c\in K\}\). A homogeneous epigraph lift is affine-linear data satisfying \(\operatorname{epi}\kappa_C=\{(x,t):t\ge0,\ \exists z,\ Ax+Bz+tc\in K\}\). The lift is semidefinite when \(K\) is a finite product of cones \(\mathbb S_+^{d_j}\) and any explicitly stated linear cones, so membership is expressed by linear matrix inequalities. Lift size comprises the auxiliary dimension and cone-block dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic gauge lift represents the unit ball or epigraph as the projection of an affine slice of a closed convex cone. An epigraph lift is homogeneous in the gauge scaling variable and includes its nonnegativity. A semidefinite gauge lift is a conic lift whose primitive cone consists of positive-semidefinite matrix cones, possibly with explicit linear components. Exactness requires the projected lifted feasible set to equal the intended ball or epigraph exactly.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A semidefinite lift can be written as finitely many linear matrix inequalities \(M_j(x,t,z)\succeq0\).
special_cases_latex: A polyhedral lift is obtained when \(K\) is a nonnegative orthant.
A second-order-cone lift is obtained when \(K\) is a product of Lorentz cones.
immediate_consequences_latex: Gauge evaluation reduces formally to minimizing \(t\) over the lifted conic epigraph.
boundary_notes: Representability does not by itself provide polynomial-time guarantees without encoding, regularity, and numerical assumptions.
A spectrahedral shadow is generally a projection, not necessarily a direct spectrahedron in the original variables.

notation.meaning: Primitive closed convex cone used in the lift.

children.top_down_role: Primitive access models used when explicit finite descriptions are unavailable.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Implicit Oracle Interface for a Gauge and Its Polar
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed and convex with \(0\in C\), let \(\kappa=\gamma_C\), and let \(C^\circ=\{y:\langle y,x\rangle\le1\ \forall x\in C\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle-based finite-dimensional access used when no finite explicit representation is supplied; both exact and tolerance-qualified interfaces are permitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An implicit gauge-polarity oracle interface is a finite specification of callable maps for \(C\), \(\kappa\), \(C^\circ\), or \(\kappa^\circ\), together with input domains, output contracts, tolerances, and costs. Admissible calls include \(\mathrm{Eval}_\kappa(x)\), \(\mathrm{Mem}_C(x)\), \(\mathrm{Sep}_C(x)\), \(\mathrm{Supp}_C(y)\), and their polar counterparts. Consistency requires \(\kappa(x)=\inf\{t\ge0:\mathrm{Mem}_C(x/t)=1\}\) and \(\kappa^\circ(y)=\sup_{x\in C}\langle y,x\rangle\), with appropriate conventions for zero scaling, infeasibility, and infinite values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An implicit gauge-polarity interface replaces a finite constraint description by declared oracle calls. Each call must specify its legal inputs, exact or approximate output, tolerance, and computational cost. The gauge-side and polar-side calls must be mutually consistent: gauge evaluation is scaling membership in the unit ball, and polar-gauge evaluation is support optimization over that ball. An interface may expose only a subset of these primitives, but it may not claim undeclared operations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak O=(\mathrm{Eval}_\kappa,\mathrm{Mem}_C,\mathrm{Sep}_C,\mathrm{Supp}_C,\mathrm{Eval}_{\kappa^\circ},\mathrm{Mem}_{C^\circ},\ldots)\) is an interface only when every included oracle has a specified and polarity-consistent contract.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Since \(\kappa^\circ=\sigma_C\), an exact support oracle for \(C\) is an exact evaluation oracle for the polar gauge.
special_cases_latex: For an atomic hull, support optimization may be implemented by maximizing over the atom set without explicitly constructing its convex hull.
immediate_consequences_latex: An optimization method using only declared calls remains meaningful even when \(C\) has no practical explicit representation.
boundary_notes: Approximate membership and weak separation require a specified norm and tolerance model.
Evaluation, membership, separation, and optimization are not automatically interchangeable without boundedness and conditioning assumptions.

notation.meaning: Specified collection of gauge and polar oracle calls.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gauge Evaluation and Scaled-Ball Membership Interface
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed and convex with \(0\in C\), and let \(\kappa_C(x)=\inf\{t\ge0:x\in tC\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact oracle access to an extended-valued finite-dimensional gauge; approximate variants require separate tolerance promises.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact gauge evaluation-membership interface consists of an evaluation oracle returning \(\kappa_C(x)\in[0,+\infty]\) and a scaled-membership oracle returning whether \(x\in tC\) for \(t\ge0\), subject to the consistency rule \(\mathrm{Mem}_C(x,t)=1\iff\kappa_C(x)\le t\). Conversely, evaluation induced by membership is \(\kappa_C(x)=\inf\{t\ge0:\mathrm{Mem}_C(x,t)=1\}\). At \(t=0\), membership means \(x\in0C\), with the convention chosen consistently with the closed perspective and recession directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This interface exposes two views of the same gauge geometry. The evaluation oracle returns the gauge value, including infinity when appropriate. The membership oracle answers whether a point lies in a specified nonnegative scaling of the unit set. Exact consistency requires membership at scale t to be equivalent to the gauge value being at most t, and the value to equal the infimum of all accepted scales. Zero scale and recession directions must be handled explicitly.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The epigraph-membership query \((x,t)\in\operatorname{epi}\kappa_C\) is the scaled-ball membership query for \(t\ge0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(C\) is the unit ball of a norm, the zero-scale query accepts only \(x=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: An exact evaluation oracle immediately implements exact scaled membership by comparison with \(t\).
boundary_notes: Binary search using membership yields approximate evaluation only when finite bounds and a numerical model are specified.
For nonabsorbing \(C\), evaluation may return \(+\infty\).
Unbounded unit sets can have nontrivial zero-gauge directions.

An exact unit-ball membership oracle receives \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and returns \(M_C(x)=1\) if \(\gamma_C(x)\le1\), and \(M_C(x)=0\) otherwise. A weak oracle with tolerance \(\delta>0\) must return inside when \(\gamma_C(x)\le1-
